In these areas lie large deserts such as the **Sahara**. Towards the poles the **Ferrel cell** follows, and after that the **polar cell**. Together they form the **three-cell model**.

abschnitte.titel: The Hadley cell and climate change
abschnitte.text: Observations since about 1980 suggest that the Hadley cells have **expanded towards the poles**. Many studies link this to **global warming**. As a result, dry areas of the subtropics could shift further towards the poles. How strongly and how fast this is happening is still being researched.

gewusst: Sailors used the steady trade winds centuries ago to cross the Atlantic.
The great deserts of the Earth often lie where the air of the Hadley cell sinks.

teile.einleitung: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on Earth and stretch for about 2,400 kilometres through South Asia. Here stands Mount Everest, the highest mountain in the world. The name comes from Sanskrit and means “abode of snow”.
wichtigste: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on Earth.
According to the measurement of 2020, Mount Everest is exactly 8,849 metres high.
Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and China.
On Earth there are 14 mountains higher than 8,000 metres.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first proven climbers to reach the summit of Everest in 1953.
“Himalaya” translated from Sanskrit means “abode of snow”.
The Himalayas formed because the Indian Plate collided with Eurasia.

abschnitte.text: The **Himalayas** lie in South Asia, between the Tibetan Plateau in the north and the Indo-Gangetic Plain in the south. They stretch across Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China. The arc is about 2,400 kilometres long. The name comes from **Sanskrit**, an ancient language of India, and means “abode of snow”.

About 50 million years ago the **Indian Plate** collided with the Eurasian Plate. The rock was pushed together and piled up enormously. This movement continues to this day, which is why the Himalayas are still growing by a few millimetres a year. That is also why strong earthquakes happen in the region again and again, as in Nepal in 2015.

**Mount Everest** lies on the border between Nepal and China. According to a joint measurement by both countries in 2020, it is **8,849 metres** high. In Nepal it is called Sagarmatha, and in Tibet Chomolungma. On Earth there are 14 mountains over 8,000 metres, the so-called **eight-thousanders**, and they all lie in the Himalayas or the neighbouring Karakoram.

On 29 May 1953 the New Zealander **Edmund Hillary** and the Sherpa **Tenzing Norgay** were the first proven climbers to stand on the summit of Everest. They were part of a British expedition. In 1956 a Swiss expedition made the first ascent of Lhotse, the fourth highest mountain in the world, and shortly afterwards the second ascent of Everest. Today hundreds of people try the climb every year, often using bottled oxygen.

Many peoples live in the Himalayas, including the **Sherpa** in Nepal, who are known as excellent mountain guides. Many people in the region are Buddhists or Hindus, and for them some mountains are sacred. Prayer flags flutter in the wind on passes and at monasteries. The kingdom of Bhutan lies almost entirely in the Himalayas.

The glaciers of the Himalayas feed big rivers such as the **Ganges**, the Indus and the Brahmaputra. Hundreds of millions of people live from this water. At the high altitudes live rare animals such as the snow leopard, the red panda and the yak. Because of global warming, many glaciers are melting, which could endanger the water supply in future.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mountain that is higher than 8,000 metres.
A people in Nepal, known as mountain guides in the Himalayas.
An ancient language from India.
The first time that people reach a summit.

gewusst: On the summit of Mount Everest you can find limestone with fossils of sea creatures.
Right at the top of Everest there is so little oxygen that this area is called the death zone.

teile.einleitung: Kangaroos are marsupials from Australia that make great leaps with their strong hind legs. They are among the best-known animals of the continent and are even shown on Australia’s coat of arms.
wichtigste: Kangaroos live in Australia and are marsupials.
They move by hopping on their hind legs.
Large kangaroos can cover up to about 9 metres in one leap.
A newborn kangaroo is only about as big as a bean.
A young one is called a “joey”.
The red kangaroo is the biggest marsupial in the world.

abschnitte.text: Kangaroos **hop** on their long, strong **hind legs**. In this way they move forward fast and far and save energy as they do so. Large kangaroos can cover up to about **9 metres** in one leap, which is as far as two cars end to end. The thick, long **tail** keeps the balance when leaping. When standing, the kangaroo also props itself on it like a third leg.

Kangaroos are **marsupials**. A newborn kangaroo is only about 2 to 3 centimetres long, as big as a bean, and weighs less than 1 gram. It climbs at once into the **pouch** on the mother’s belly. There it goes on growing for many months, until it is big enough to look out and finally to hop out. A young kangaroo is called a **“joey”**.

Kangaroos are **herbivores**. They eat mainly grasses, herbs and leaves. Many species are active at dusk and in the night, when it is cooler. By day they often rest in the shade. Kangaroos usually live together in groups called a **mob**.

Male kangaroos sometimes test their strength. They stand up and **box** with their front legs. In doing so they prop themselves on their tail and **kick** with their strong hind legs. The **red kangaroo** is the biggest marsupial alive today. A male standing upright can be as tall as an adult human.

gewusst: On Australia’s coat of arms a kangaroo and an emu hold the shield.
There are many species of kangaroo, and the smallest are not much bigger than a rabbit.

teile.einleitung: **Israel** is a small country in the Middle East, at the eastern end of the Mediterranean. It was founded in 1948 and has very varied landscapes: coast, hills, desert and the Dead Sea. The region is of great importance for Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
wichtigste: Israel lies on the Mediterranean in the west.
The main language is **Hebrew**.
The money is called the **shekel**.
On the flag you can see a blue **Star of David**.
In the south lies the **Negev** desert, and at the very south the town of Eilat on the Red Sea.
Tel Aviv is the most important economic centre.

abschnitte.text: Israel borders the **Mediterranean** in the west. In the north lies the freshwater lake, the **Sea of Galilee**, from which the Jordan flows south. In the east lies the **Dead Sea**, so salty that you float on top almost by yourself. Its shore is the lowest place on land on the whole Earth. The south is covered by the **Negev** desert, at whose tip the town of **Eilat** lies on the Red Sea.

**Tel Aviv** on the Mediterranean is a modern big city and the most important economic centre. **Haifa** in the north is a port city on Mount Carmel, known for its terraced gardens. **Jerusalem** is holy to three religions. Israel regards Jerusalem as its capital city, but internationally the status of the city is disputed, and many states have their embassies in Tel Aviv.

Most people speak **Hebrew**, a very old language that was revived as an everyday language in the 19th and 20th centuries. Many people also speak Arabic. People pay with the **shekel**. The flag is white with two blue stripes and a blue **Star of David** in the middle, a symbol of Judaism.

Israel was founded in 1948. Since then there have been conflicts with neighbouring countries and above all with the **Palestinians**, who also live in this region and want a state of their own. There have been several wars and many attempts to make peace. What a fair solution should look like is very disputed and is discussed worldwide.

gewusst: The Dead Sea is almost ten times as salty as the Mediterranean.
In the Dead Sea there are hardly any living things apart from tiny microbes, because of all the salt.

teile.einleitung: A large city is a city with a great many inhabitants. People usually speak of a large city from 100,000 people. There is a lot going on there, and there are blocks of flats, offices, shops and a lot of traffic.
wichtigste: A city with 100,000 inhabitants or more is usually called a large city.
Many people live there in blocks of flats.
In the city centre, many shops, offices and restaurants lie close together.
When very many cars drive at the same time, traffic jams often form.
Giant cities exist on all continents, for example London, Mumbai, Lagos, São Paulo and Shanghai.

abschnitte.text: A city with at least **100,000 inhabitants** is usually called a **large city**. In Switzerland these include, for example, Zurich, Geneva, Basel, Lausanne, Bern and Winterthur. Compared with cities in other countries, though, they are rather small. Cities with many millions of people are called **million cities** or **megacities**. Often a city and its suburbs grow together into a large **urban area**.

In large cities space is scarce. That is why many families live in **blocks of flats**, that is, big buildings with many flats on top of one another. This way many people fit onto little ground. In the **city centre**, especially many shops, offices, restaurants and theatres lie close together. On the edge of the city there are often residential districts, factories and shopping centres.

Every day, very many people are on the move in a large city. When too many cars drive at the same time, they hardly move forward, and a **traffic jam** forms. That is why **buses, trams, underground trains** and cycle paths are important. Many big cities have a dense network of trains, also underground. In Zurich, for example, many people travel by tram and S-Bahn.

There are huge cities on all continents. **London** lies on the Thames and is the capital of Great Britain. **Mumbai** lies on the west coast of India, and **Shanghai** on the east coast of China. **São Paulo** is the biggest city in Brazil, and **Lagos** in Nigeria is one of the biggest cities in Africa. In each of these cities live many millions of people, more than in the whole of Switzerland.

gewusst: Today more than half of all people in the world live in cities.
In some giant cities more people live than in the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Grand Canyon is a huge gorge in the south-west of the USA. The Colorado River has carved it into the rock over many millions of years. Today it is one of the most famous landscapes in the world.
wichtigste: The Grand Canyon lies in the US state of Arizona.
The Colorado River carved out the gorge.
The gorge is about 450 kilometres long.
At its deepest points it is about 1.8 kilometres deep.
The Grand Canyon has been a national park since 1919.
The layers of rock show almost 2 billion years of Earth’s history.

abschnitte.text: A **canyon** is a deep gorge with steep walls, and “grand” means big. The Grand Canyon lies in the state of **Arizona**. It is about 450 kilometres long and in some places many kilometres wide. At its deepest points it drops about 1800 metres. That is roughly the height of the Rigi above sea level. If you want to drive from the south rim to the north rim, you have to drive about 350 kilometres around the gorge.

Right at the bottom of the gorge flows the **Colorado River**. It carries sand and stones along with it, which work like sandpaper. In this way it has cut deeper and deeper into the rock over **many millions of years**. At the same time the land slowly rose, which made the cutting stronger. Rain, frost and wind also wear the walls away further. That is why the canyon is so wide and has so many steps and towers.

In the walls lie many **layers of rock** on top of one another, like the pages of a book. The lowest ones are almost **two billion years** old, and the top ones much younger. In some layers researchers find **fossils** of sea creatures. This shows that there used to be sea here. The Grand Canyon is therefore very valuable for **geology**, because hardly anywhere else can you see so much of Earth’s history at once.

The rock walls glow mainly **red, orange and brown**. Especially in the morning and evening the colours change a great deal. Pine trees grow on the rim, while down by the river it is hot and dry. In the area live animals such as deer, lizards and large birds of prey. For a long time **Indigenous peoples** have also lived there, for example the Havasupai.

Since **1919** the Grand Canyon has been a **national park**, so that nature stays protected. Since 1979 it has also been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Millions of people come every year. Most visit the south rim with its viewpoints. Some hike down steep paths or travel through the gorge in boats on the Colorado River.

gewusst: The oldest rocks at the very bottom of the canyon are almost half as old as the Earth itself.
At the bottom of the gorge it is often much hotter in summer than up on the rim.

teile.einleitung: The Great Ocean Road is a famous road on the south coast of Australia. It passes cliffs, beaches and forests. It was built by soldiers who had come home from the First World War.
wichtigste: The Great Ocean Road lies in the state of Victoria in Australia.
It begins west of Melbourne.
The road is about 240 kilometres long.
Returned soldiers built it from 1919.
The rock stacks of the Twelve Apostles are well known.
Wild koalas live in the eucalyptus trees.

abschnitte.text: The Great Ocean Road runs right along the coast. It lies in the south of Australia in the state of **Victoria** and begins west of **Melbourne**. The road is about **240 kilometres** long. It winds past cliffs, sandy beaches and small towns. Many people drive it by car or bus and often stop to enjoy the view.

The road was built from **1919** by **soldiers** who had come back from the First World War. They often worked with shovels, picks and by hand. This gave them work, and the remote places on the coast became easier to reach. The road is also a **memorial** to the soldiers who died in the war. It is therefore called the largest war memorial in the world.

Best known are the **Twelve Apostles**. These are tall stacks of **limestone** standing in the sea. The waves washed them out of the coast. The sea keeps gnawing at them, and every now and then a stack collapses. That is why there are now fewer than twelve. At the same time, new stacks can form from the coast.

Along the route there are rainforests and **eucalyptus forests**. Wild **koalas** live there, spending many hours asleep in the trees. You can also see kangaroos, colourful parrots and other birds. In the sea off the coast, whales sometimes pass by in winter.

gewusst: The Great Ocean Road is regarded as the largest war memorial in the world.
Of the Twelve Apostles there are now fewer than twelve standing, because the sea has brought some of them down.

teile.einleitung: Indonesia is a country in South-East Asia and the biggest island state in the world. It consists of over 17,000 islands, through which the equator runs. Here there are rainforests, volcanoes and rare animals such as the Komodo dragon.
wichtigste: With over 17,000 islands, Indonesia is the biggest island state in the world.
The biggest city is Jakarta on the island of Java.
On Borneo, Indonesia is building the new capital city, Nusantara.
The equator runs through the middle of the country, so it is always warm.
The Komodo dragon is the biggest lizard in the world.
The currency is called the rupiah.

abschnitte.text: Indonesia has **over 17,000 islands**, but on many of them nobody lives. The biggest include **Sumatra**, **Java** and parts of **Borneo**. The **equator** runs through the middle of the country, so it is warm all year round. Indonesia is one of the most populous countries in the world. Most people are Muslims.

The biggest city is **Jakarta** on the island of Java. It has long been the capital city. Jakarta, however, is overcrowded and is sinking in places. That is why Indonesia is building a new capital city in the east of Borneo, called **Nusantara**. Across the whole country people pay with the **rupiah**.

Indonesia lies on the **Pacific Ring of Fire**. That is why there are very many volcanoes and also earthquakes there. Famous is **Krakatoa**, between Java and Sumatra. When it erupted in **1883**, the bang could be heard very far away. The ash of the volcanoes also makes the soils very fertile, for example for **rice fields**.

On a few islands lives the **Komodo dragon**, the biggest lizard in the world. It can grow to about 3 metres long. In the rainforests of Sumatra and Borneo live **orangutans**. Their name means “person of the forest”. Because a lot of rainforest is cleared for plantations, orangutans are now seriously threatened.

On Java stands the huge Buddhist temple of **Borobudur** from the 9th century. It is decorated with over 2,600 reliefs and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Very popular with holidaymakers is the island of **Bali** with its beaches, rice fields and many temples. Every year millions of visitors come, including from Switzerland.

gewusst: Indonesia’s motto is “Unity in Diversity”, because hundreds of languages are spoken in the country.
Indonesia declared its independence from the Netherlands in 1945.

teile.einleitung: The Great Blue Hole is a perfectly round, deep blue hole in the sea off the coast of Belize in Central America. From the air it looks like a dark eye in the middle of the turquoise water.
wichtigste: The Great Blue Hole lies in Lighthouse Reef off the coast of Belize.
It is about 300 metres wide and over 120 metres deep.
It formed in the Ice Age as a cave whose roof later collapsed.
The marine explorer Jacques-Yves Cousteau made it famous.
It is part of the protected Belize Barrier Reef.

abschnitte.text: The Great Blue Hole lies in the middle of a ring of coral, the **Lighthouse Reef**. All around, the water is shallow and turquoise. In the hole, by contrast, it is over **120 metres** deep, which is why it looks dark blue. The hole is almost perfectly round and about **300 metres** wide. Holes like this are called **blue holes**.

During the **Ice Age** the sea level was much lower than today. At that time the area was dry land made of limestone. Rainwater dissolved the limestone, and a large **cave** formed. At some point its roof collapsed. When the ice melted and the sea rose, the cave filled with water. Deep down you can still find **stalactites and stalagmites**, which could only have grown in the air.

The hole became well known through the French marine explorer **Jacques-Yves Cousteau**, who studied it in the 1970s. Today many divers come. Deep down the water has very little oxygen, so there is hardly any life there. The Blue Hole is part of the **Belize Barrier Reef**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: The stalactites and stalagmites in the Great Blue Hole prove that this was once dry land.

teile.einleitung: Hispaniola is a large island in the Caribbean. Two states share the island: Haiti in the west and the Dominican Republic in the east. The island got its name from Christopher Columbus.
wichtigste: Hispaniola is an island in the Caribbean.
Haiti lies in the west, and the larger Dominican Republic in the east.
Columbus reached the island in 1492 and called it “La Isla Española”.
From this came the name Hispaniola.
Before the Spanish arrived, the Taíno lived there.

abschnitte.text: **Hispaniola** belongs to the Greater Antilles in the Caribbean. After Cuba it is the second biggest island in the region. Two states share the island. In the west lies **Haiti**, and in the larger east the **Dominican Republic**. In Haiti people speak French and Haitian Creole, and in the Dominican Republic Spanish.

In **1492** **Christopher Columbus** reached the island. He called it **“La Isla Española”**, that is, the Spanish island. From this came the name **Hispaniola**. At that time the **Taíno** lived on the island. Under Spanish rule, very many of them died from diseases brought in from outside and from hard forced labour.

Later the west of the island came under **French** rule, while the east stayed **Spanish**. That is why the two parts developed differently. The west became independent in **1804** as Haiti. The Dominican Republic became a state of its own a few decades later. The two countries still differ in language and culture today.

gewusst: On Hispaniola lies the highest mountain in the Caribbean, Pico Duarte in the Dominican Republic.

teile.einleitung: The Hawaiian hotspot is a place deep inside the Earth where hot rock rises and forms volcanoes. The Pacific Plate moves across it. This created a long chain of islands and underwater mountains that get older the further they lie from the hotspot.
wichtigste: A hotspot is an almost fixed source of melt in the Earth’s mantle.
The Pacific Plate moves north-west over the hotspot at about 7 to 10 cm a year.
The further north-west a Hawaiian island lies, the older it is.
The Emperor Seamounts continue the chain to the north, and the whole chain is about 6000 km long.
The bend in the chain is about 47 million years old.
J. Tuzo Wilson explained the islands with a hotspot in 1963.
The youngest volcano is the underwater volcano Kamaʻehuakanaloa.

abschnitte.text: Under Hawaii, hot rock rises from great depth. This is called a **mantle plume**. According to a widespread hypothesis it comes from the **core-mantle boundary**, that is, from the boundary between the Earth’s core and the Earth’s mantle. Seismic images show a hot zone reaching deep down under Hawaii. Where the rock melts, magma forms and breaks through the seabed as a **volcano**.

The hotspot stays almost in the same place. The **Pacific Plate**, however, moves north-west at about **7 to 10 cm a year**. So the volcanoes are carried away from the hotspot over time and become extinct. That is why the islands become **older** towards the north-west. **Kauaʻi** is about 5 million years old, and the island of **Hawaiʻi** less than 1 million years. There, for example, **Kīlauea** is very active. In 2018 its lava destroyed over 700 buildings in the **Puna** region.

The trail of volcanoes reaches far beyond today’s islands. The **Hawaiian-Emperor chain** is about **6000 km** long. Its northern part, the **Emperor Seamounts**, reaches as far as the Aleutian Trench. Between the two parts there is a clear **bend**, dated to about **47 million years** ago. It shows that the plate’s movement changed or that the hotspot itself moved.

Old volcanic islands slowly sink and are worn away by the sea. In warm water, **corals** grow upwards and form **atolls**. The further north, the cooler the water and the more slowly the corals grow. From the **Darwin Point**, near **Kure Atoll**, they can no longer keep up with the sinking. The atolls then sink into flat underwater mountains, the **guyots**.

The Canadian geologist **John Tuzo Wilson** explained in **1963** the sequence of ages of the islands as the trail of a plate moving over a fixed source of melt. **W. Jason Morgan** added the idea of mantle plumes in **1971**. South-east of the island of Hawaiʻi a new volcano is already growing: the seamount **Kamaʻehuakanaloa**, formerly **Lōʻihi**. It still lies about 1000 m below sea level and was renamed in 2021.

gewusst: The chain of islands of Hawaii works like a conveyor belt: new volcanoes form in the south-east, and old ones disappear into the sea in the north-west.
In the distant future, in many tens of thousands of years, Kamaʻehuakanaloa could stick out of the sea as a new island.

teile.einleitung: Guadeloupe is a group of islands in the Caribbean that belongs to France. On the map its two main islands look like a butterfly. People pay there with the euro.
wichtigste: Guadeloupe is a French overseas department in the Caribbean.
The two main islands are called Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre.
Together they have the shape of a butterfly.
On Basse-Terre stands the volcano La Soufrière.
Guadeloupe belongs to the European Union, and people pay with the euro.

abschnitte.text: Guadeloupe consists of two main islands: **Basse-Terre** in the west and **Grande-Terre** in the east. They are separated only by a narrow arm of the sea. On the map they look together like the **wings of a butterfly**. Basse-Terre is mountainous and covered with rainforest. Grande-Terre is flatter and has many sandy beaches. Smaller islands such as Marie-Galante and Les Saintes also belong to it.

On Basse-Terre stands the volcano **La Soufrière**. It is the highest mountain in the Lesser Antilles and is still active. Around the volcano lies a **national park** with rainforest and waterfalls. The fertility of the volcanic soil is good for bananas and sugar cane. Rum is also made from sugar cane.

Guadeloupe is an **overseas department** of France. This means it also belongs to the **European Union**, and people pay with the **euro**. The official language is French, and many people also speak a **Creole language**. Christopher Columbus came here in 1493. He named the island after a monastery in Spain.

gewusst: On Guadeloupe people pay with the euro, although the islands lie in the middle of the Caribbean.

teile.einleitung: The **Isla del Sol**, the “Island of the Sun”, lies in **Lake Titicaca** in South America, on the Bolivian side. According to an Inca legend, the Sun was born here. On the island there are ancient ruins and terraced fields.
wichtigste: The Isla del Sol lies in Lake Titicaca in Bolivia.
According to the Inca legend it is the birthplace of the Sun.
Lake Titicaca lies at about 3,800 metres above sea level.
On the island there are ruins from the time of the Incas.
There are no cars on the island, and people go on foot.

abschnitte.text: According to an old legend of the **Incas**, the Sun rose out of the lake on this island. The first Inca rulers, **Manco Cápac** and **Mama Ocllo**, are also said to have set out from here to found their empire. For the Incas the island was therefore a sacred place. Pilgrims came from far away to pray here.

**Lake Titicaca** lies high in the Andes between Bolivia and Peru, at about 3,800 metres above sea level. It is considered the highest navigable lake on Earth. The Isla del Sol is one of the biggest islands in the lake. You reach it by boat, usually from the little town of **Copacabana**.

On the island stand ruins from the time of the Incas, such as a stone labyrinth called **Chincana** and the building **Pilko Kaina**. On the steep slopes you can see many **terraces**, on which people have grown potatoes, maize and other plants for centuries. Today people live in some villages, and they often speak Aymara. There are no cars, and paths lead across the island on foot.

gewusst: Very close by lies the smaller Isla de la Luna, the “Island of the Moon”.
Because of the altitude, visitors quickly get out of breath climbing the steps on the island.

teile.einleitung: The Americas stretch from the far north to the southern tip of South America. Their capitals are very different: some were founded by the Spanish, others newly planned, and some lie high in the Andes.
wichtigste: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay and lies on the Río de la Plata.
Brasília was newly built and inaugurated in 1960.
La Paz in Bolivia is the highest seat of government in the world.
Bogotá is the capital of Colombia, and Caracas is the capital of Venezuela.
Havana is the capital of Cuba, and its old town is a World Heritage Site.
Santiago is the capital of Chile.
Lima is the capital of Peru and was founded in 1535.

abschnitte.text: Brazil’s capital used to be in **Rio de Janeiro** on the coast. To strengthen the interior of the country, **Brasília** was newly built in just a few years and inaugurated in **1960**. The city was planned in detail. From the air its layout looks like an **aeroplane** or a bird. Many of its buildings are modern works by the architect Oscar Niemeyer.

Several capitals lie in the **Andes**. **La Paz** in Bolivia lies at about **3600 metres** above sea level and is the highest seat of government in the world. The constitutional capital of Bolivia, however, is **Sucre**. **Bogotá**, the capital of Colombia, lies at about 2600 metres. **Santiago**, the capital of Chile, lies in a valley in front of the Andes. More than a third of all Chileans live in the Greater Santiago area.

**Lima** lies on the Pacific coast and was founded by the Spanish in **1535**. **Cusco** used to be the capital of the Inca empire. **Montevideo** lies on the south coast of **Uruguay** on the **Río de la Plata**. Well over a third of the country’s inhabitants live there. **Havana** on the north coast of **Cuba** has an old town that is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

Some capitals are easily mixed up. **Caracas** is the capital of **Venezuela**, not of Colombia. In Bolivia, **La Paz** and **Sucre** share the tasks. And in Brazil the capital is not the well-known city of Rio de Janeiro, but **Brasília**.

gewusst: In La Paz the air is so thin that visitors often get out of breath at first even climbing stairs.
Brasília was planned and built as a whole before most people lived there.

teile.einleitung: Sclerophyll (hard-leaved) vegetation grows in areas with a Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, damp winters. The plants have hard, leathery leaves that protect them from water loss. Typical are the olive tree, the holm oak, the cork oak and fragrant herbs.
wichtigste: Sclerophyll plants have small, leathery, evergreen leaves with a thick layer of wax.
These leaves reduce evaporation in the dry summers.
The climate is called the Mediterranean climate: winter rain and summer drought.
The holm oak used to form large forests, and the olive tree is the typical cultivated plant.
Cork is obtained from the bark of the cork oak.
Maquis is dense scrubland, and garrigue is low shrubland on poor soils.
A Mediterranean climate also exists in California, Chile, South Africa and Australia.

abschnitte.text: In the **Mediterranean climate** the summers are hot and dry, and the winters mild and damp. In winter, low-pressure areas of the **westerly wind belt** bring rain. In summer, subtropical **high-pressure areas** lie over the region, and for weeks it hardly rains. This climate is also called the **Etesian climate**. It exists not only on the Mediterranean, but also in **California**, central Chile, the south-west of South Africa and parts of Australia.

The plants have to survive the dry summers. Their leaves are small, **leathery** and **evergreen**. They have a thick, often waxy outer skin through which little water evaporates. That is why these plants are called **sclerophylls**. Because they do not shed their leaves, they can keep growing in the mild winter.

The **holm oak** with its small, leathery leaves used to form large forests. These were heavily cut down over the centuries. The **olive tree** has been grown around the Mediterranean for thousands of years and can become very old. From the thick bark of the **cork oak**, **cork** is obtained. It can be stripped roughly every nine years without the tree dying. Portugal is the biggest cork producer in the world.

Where the forests disappeared, **maquis** often grew. This is dense scrubland with shrubs up to several metres high, such as strawberry tree, myrtle and tree heath. On very poor limestone soils, for example in southern France, **garrigue** grows. It is lower and patchier. There, herbs such as **thyme**, **rosemary** and **lavender** give off their scent. In California similar scrubland is called **chaparral**.

In summer the plants are very parched from heat and drought. Many sclerophyll plants also contain flammable **essential oils**. That is why **forest and bush fires** are frequent in the Mediterranean region. Some plants are adapted to this and sprout again after a fire.

gewusst: The scent of the garrigue on hot days comes from the essential oils of the herbs, which evaporate in the heat.
Olive trees can be several hundred years old, and some even over a thousand years.

teile.einleitung: A hygrometer is an instrument for measuring humidity. It shows how much water vapour is in the air. It is needed by weather services, but also at home, in museums and in greenhouses.
wichtigste: A hygrometer is used to measure humidity.
Usually it shows the relative humidity as a percentage.
The hair hygrometer makes use of the fact that hairs get longer in damp air.
The Geneva scientist Horace-Bénédict de Saussure built a well-known hair hygrometer.
Today many hygrometers work with electronic sensors.

abschnitte.text: Air always contains some **water vapour**, which you cannot see. Warm air can take up more water vapour than cold air. The **relative humidity** states, as a percentage, how much water vapour is in the air compared with the greatest amount it can hold at that temperature. At 100 per cent the air is saturated, and then fog or dew forms.

Human hair gets a little **longer** in damp air and shorter again in dry air. In a **hair hygrometer** a hair is attached to a pointer. If the length of the hair changes, the pointer moves. A well-known hair hygrometer was built in the 18th century by the Geneva naturalist **Horace-Bénédict de Saussure**.

With a **psychrometer** two thermometers are compared. One is dry, and the other is wrapped in a damp cloth. Because water cools as it evaporates, the damp thermometer shows a lower reading. From the difference the humidity is worked out. Today many instruments use **electronic sensors**, which are very precise and small.

Weather services such as **MeteoSwiss** measure humidity at many stations. In homes a hygrometer helps with airing a room properly: if the air is too damp, **mould** can form. If it is too dry, the eyes and throat become irritated. In museums too, the right humidity is important so that pictures and wood do not come to harm.

gewusst: The name comes from Greek: “hygros” means damp, and “metron” means measure.
Indoors, a relative humidity of about 40 to 60 per cent is considered pleasant.

teile.einleitung: An **inselberg** is a mountain that rises alone and steeply from a wide, flat plain. It looks like an island in a sea of land. Such mountains are found mainly in the tropics and in desert regions. The word is German and means “island mountain”.
wichtigste: An inselberg rises alone out of a plain.
The term was coined by the German geologist **Wilhelm Bornhardt** during research in East Africa.
Inselbergs typically form above **peneplains** in the seasonally wet and dry tropics.
Inselbergs usually consist of especially hard rock, for example granite.
The well-known Uluru in Australia is often described as an inselberg.

abschnitte.text: If you stand on the plain, you can see the inselberg from far away. All around, the land is flat, and suddenly a rock rises steeply. The name fits well: the mountain lies in the landscape like an island in the water. The plain around it is often a **peneplain**, that is, an area that has been worn almost completely flat over a very long time.

Inselbergs form over millions of years. In the **seasonally wet and dry tropics**, where a rainy season and a dry season alternate, water breaks down the rock deep in the ground. Soft rock is worn away in the process, and hard rock is left standing. What remains are single blocks of hard rock that now rise from the plain as inselbergs. The term comes from **Wilhelm Bornhardt**, who studied such mountains in East Africa.

Inselbergs are found in Africa, South America, India and Australia. Very famous is **Uluru** in central Australia, a huge red rock made of sandstone. For the Aboriginal people, the original inhabitants of Australia, it is a sacred place. In the Namib and the Sahara too, many single rocky mountains stand in wide plains.

gewusst: Inselbergs can rise several hundred metres above the plain.
Because they offer rain and shade, more plants often grow at their foot than in the plain all around.

teile.einleitung: The Human Development Index, or HDI, compares how well people live in different countries. It measures not only money, but also health and education. The UN publishes it every year.
wichtigste: The HDI appears in the Human Development Report of the UNDP.
The first report with the HDI appeared in 1990.
It combines the three areas of health, education and standard of living.
Since 2010 the sub-indices have been combined using the geometric mean.
From a value of 0.800, a country counts as “very high” in development.
The IHDI also takes account of inequality within a country.

abschnitte.text: The HDI is published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**. The first **Human Development Report** appeared in **1990**. The index was developed under the leadership of the Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq**. The Nobel Prize winner **Amartya Sen** helped. For him, development means that people have more opportunities to shape their own lives.

The HDI measures three areas. For **health**, **life expectancy at birth** counts. For **education**, what counts is how many years people go to school. For the **standard of living** it uses **gross national income per head** in **purchasing power parity**. Income goes in as a logarithm, so that extra income in rich countries counts for less.

Each area gives a sub-index between 0 and 1. Since **2010** the three have been combined using the **geometric mean**. In this way a weak area cannot be fully made up for by a strong one. An example: with 1.0, 0.8 and 0.64 the product is 0.512, and the cube root of that gives an HDI of **0.8**.

The UNDP divides countries into four groups: **low** below 0.550, **medium**, **high** from 0.700 and **very high** from 0.800. **Switzerland** has been among the countries with the highest HDI for many years. In the 2023/2024 report it was in first place. Since 2010 there has also been the **IHDI**, which lowers the value the more unequally health, education and income are distributed.

gewusst: The HDI shows that two countries with the same income can do very differently, depending on health and education.
At the bottom of the ranking there are usually countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

teile.einleitung: High-speed trains run faster than 200 km/h and link big cities in a few hours. It all began in 1964 in Japan. Today such trains exist in many countries, and China has the biggest network.
wichtigste: In 1964 Japan opened the first high-speed line in the world with the Shinkansen.
The first line, the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, links Tokyo and Osaka.
A French TGV reached about 575 km/h in 2007, a record for trains with wheels.
A Japanese maglev train even ran at 603 km/h in 2015.
China has by far the longest high-speed network in the world.
Under the EU definition, trains on newly built lines must reach at least 250 km/h.
Over distances of about 300 to 800 km, trains are often as fast as aeroplanes.

abschnitte.text: The first **high-speed line** in the world was opened by **Japan** in **1964**, shortly before the Olympic Games in Tokyo. The train is called the **Shinkansen**. The first line, the **Tōkaidō Shinkansen**, links **Tokyo** and **Osaka**, the two biggest urban areas in the country. At first the train ran at up to 210 km/h. The line is still one of the most heavily used high-speed lines in the world.

In April **2007** a French **TGV** set a record. The test train V150 reached **574.8 km/h** on the LGV Est line. This is still the record for trains with wheels on rails. Even faster are **maglev trains**, which float on a magnetic field without touching the track. The Japanese **SCMaglev** even reached **603 km/h** in **2015**. It is to run between Tokyo and Nagoya in future.

**China** began building a high-speed network in **2008**. By **2023** it had grown to over **40,000 km**, more than all other countries together. In South-East Asia, **Indonesia** opened the first high-speed railway in the region in **2023**. It links **Jakarta** and **Bandung** over about 140 km. In Europe there are big networks, for example, in France, Spain, Germany and Italy.

abschnitte.titel: When is a train fast enough?
abschnitte.text: The **EU** has set out what counts as high speed. On **newly built lines**, trains must reach at least **250 km/h**. On upgraded older lines about **200 km/h** is enough. In **Switzerland**, trains run, for example, through the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** at up to 200 km/h. Swiss passengers can also travel to Paris on the TGV.

Over distances of about **300 to 800 km**, high-speed trains often replace domestic flights. Stations are usually in the **city centre**. Air travellers, by contrast, have to travel to the airport, go through checks and wait. From city centre to city centre the train is therefore often just as fast or faster. It also usually uses less energy per passenger.

gewusst: Because of its long, pointed nose, the Shinkansen is often called the “bullet train”.
At 300 km/h a train covers more than 80 metres in one second.

teile.einleitung: **Iran** is a large country in Western Asia, between the Caspian Sea in the north and the Persian Gulf in the south. In the West it used to be called **Persia**. The country has a very old culture and is famous for carpets, saffron and magnificent mosques.
wichtigste: The capital city of Iran is **Tehran**.
In the past the country was called Persia in the West.
The most important language is **Persian**, also called Farsi.
Iran is famous for carpets, saffron and pistachios.
Persepolis was a royal city of the ancient Persian kings.
The New Year festival **Nowruz** is celebrated at the beginning of spring.

abschnitte.text: Iran consists for a large part of a dry **plateau**. In the west and south the **Zagros Mountains** stretch through the country, and in the north lie the Alborz Mountains with the volcano **Damavand**, the highest mountain in Iran. In the interior there are large salt and sand deserts. In the north Iran borders the Caspian Sea, and in the south the Persian Gulf.

About 2,500 years ago the Persian great kings ruled over a huge empire. Their magnificent royal city was **Persepolis**, whose ruins are now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There you can still see columns and reliefs of people from many nations bringing gifts. Until 1935 the country was mostly called Persia in the West, and then the name Iran came into use.

The capital city **Tehran** is a huge city at the foot of the mountains. Also very famous is **Isfahan**, with a vast square surrounded by mosques with blue tiles and domes. Persian **carpets** have been knotted by hand for a long time and are sold all over the world. Poetry too has a long tradition in Iran.

Iran grows very many **pistachios** and supplies the greatest part of the world’s **saffron**. Saffron is an expensive spice made from the threads of a crocus flower. The most important festival is **Nowruz**, the Persian New Year at the beginning of spring, around 21 March. Then families visit each other, and a table is laid with seven things whose names begin with the same letter.

Since the revolution of 1979 Iran has been an **Islamic Republic**. Religion plays a big part in the state, and a religious leader holds the highest power. Most people are Shia Muslims. But Christians, Jews, Zoroastrians and other groups also live in the country.

gewusst: For one kilogram of saffron you need the threads of over a hundred thousand flowers.
Nowruz is celebrated not only in Iran, but in many countries of Central Asia.

teile.einleitung: Huascarán is the highest mountain in Peru. It lies in the Cordillera Blanca, a glaciated range of the Andes. At about 6,770 metres it is the highest mountain in the tropics.
wichtigste: Huascarán is the highest mountain in Peru.
Its higher south summit is about 6,770 metres high.
It lies in the Cordillera Blanca, the “white range” of the Andes.
It is the highest mountain in the tropics.
Around the mountain lies a national park that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: Huascarán has two summits: the higher **south summit** at about 6,770 metres and the somewhat lower **north summit**. It lies in the **Cordillera Blanca**, which means “white range” in Spanish. The name comes from the many glaciers. Although the mountain lies close to the equator, its summit is covered with snow and ice all year round.

Around the mountain lies **Huascarán National Park**. It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In the park there are glaciers, turquoise mountain lakes and rare plants such as the giant **Puya raimondii**. Many mountaineers and hikers from all over the world come here, including from Switzerland.

On Huascarán, large masses of ice and rock can break loose. In **1970** a strong earthquake set off a huge **avalanche**. It almost completely destroyed the town of **Yungay** in the valley. Today experts watch the glaciers closely, also because they are melting due to climate change.

gewusst: The Puya raimondii in the national park can form a flower spike more than 10 metres high.

teile.einleitung: Wood is the firm part of trees and shrubs. It is one of the oldest raw materials used by people and is used for building, heating and making paper. Because trees grow back, wood is called a renewable raw material.
wichtigste: Wood comes from trees and is obtained mainly from the trunks.
The annual rings in the trunk show how old a tree is.
Paper and cardboard are made from wood fibres.
About a third of Switzerland is covered with forest.
The spruce is the most common tree in the Swiss forest.
Forestry workers look after the forest and fell trees, and in the sawmill these are turned into planks.
Balsa wood is very light and suitable for model aeroplanes.

abschnitte.text: **Wood** is the firm, hard part of trees and shrubs. It is obtained mainly from the **trunks**. Every year a new layer grows in the trunk. In a cross-section you can see these layers as **annual rings**. If you count the rings, you know how old the tree is. Wide rings show good years, and narrow rings show rather dry or cold years.

About **a third** of the area of Switzerland is **forest**. Most of it lies in the **Jura**, the **Pre-Alps** and the **Alps**. The most common tree is the **spruce**. Its wood is often used for building. In the mountains the forest also protects villages and roads from **avalanches** and falling rocks.

abschnitte.titel: From the forest to the plank
abschnitte.text: **Forestry workers** work in the forest. They fell trees, plant new ones and look after the forest. The trunks then go to the **sawmill**. There big saws cut them into **planks** and **beams**. After that the wood has to dry, so that it does not warp later.

From wood people build houses, furniture and toys. They burn it for **heating**. For **paper** and **cardboard**, wood is broken down into fine fibres and turned into a pulp. There are very different kinds of wood. **Balsa wood** comes from a tree from South America. It is especially light and easy to cut, which is why it is used for **model aeroplanes**.

Wood is called a **renewable raw material**. When trees are felled, new trees can grow in their place. If the forest is looked after well and no more wood is cut than grows back, the wood does not run out. In Switzerland this is laid down in the forest law: the area of forest must not get smaller.

gewusst: Since 1876 a federal law has protected the forest in parts of Switzerland from clear-cutting.
Compared with its weight, wood is surprisingly strong, and is therefore also used for large buildings.

teile.einleitung: Camels are perfectly adapted to life in the desert. They can go a long time without water and carry people and loads through sand and heat.
wichtigste: Camels eat plants, even thorny and salty ones.
In the hump fat is stored, not water.
The camel is also called the ship of the desert.
Long eyelashes and nostrils that can be closed protect against sand.
Broad feet stop them from sinking into the sand.
A thirsty camel drinks a great deal all at once.

abschnitte.text: There are two well-known species of camel. The **dromedary** has one hump and lives mainly in North Africa and Arabia. The **Bactrian camel** has two humps and lives in the cold steppes and deserts of Central Asia. Because camels sway back and forth as they walk, they are called **ships of the desert**. For thousands of years they have carried people and loads.

Many people believe there is water in the hump. That is not true: the hump consists of **fat**. The camel can live off this when there is hardly any food. If it is not fed for a long time, the hump becomes smaller and can even flop over to the side. Camels eat **plants** such as grasses and leaves, even thorny and salty ones. Their tough mouth is hardly bothered by the thorns.

In the desert there are often **sandstorms**. Camels have long, dense **eyelashes** that keep sand and dust out of the eyes. They can close their **nostrils** so that no sand gets in. Their ears are also protected with hairs. Their **broad, soft feet** spread the weight like snowshoes, so they hardly sink into the sand.

Camels can go a very long time without water. They sweat little and lose only a little water. Their body temperature may rise higher during the day than in many other animals. When a thirsty camel finds water, it drinks **a great deal all at once**, a huge amount in only about ten minutes. In this way it quickly replaces the water it has lost.

gewusst: In Australia many wild dromedaries live. Their ancestors were brought there in the past as pack animals and later set free.
Camel milk is drunk in some countries and is also made into cheese and chocolate.

teile.einleitung: **Iraq** is a country in Western Asia, in the area between the rivers Euphrates and Tigris. Here lay ancient **Mesopotamia**, where thousands of years ago some of the first cities and writing came into being. The capital city is **Baghdad**.
wichtigste: The capital city of Iraq is Baghdad.
Baghdad was founded in the year 762 by the **Abbasids**.
The official languages are Arabic and Kurdish.
Basra is the most important port of the country.
Iraq has only a short access to the Persian Gulf.
Najaf is an important place of pilgrimage for Shia Muslims.

abschnitte.text: Through Iraq flow the great rivers **Euphrates** and **Tigris**. The Greeks called the region **Mesopotamia**, which means “land between the rivers”. Here lived the Sumerians and Babylonians. They built early cities such as Ur and Babylon, invented **cuneiform writing** and irrigated their fields with canals. Many experts therefore call the area a cradle of civilisation.

The city of **Baghdad** on the Tigris was founded in the year 762 by the ruling family of the **Abbasids**. In the Middle Ages it was one of the biggest and richest cities in the world. There many books were translated, and sciences such as mathematics and medicine were cultivated. The stories of “One Thousand and One Nights” are also often set in Baghdad. Today Baghdad is the capital city and biggest city of Iraq.

Most people in Iraq speak **Arabic**. In the north live many **Kurds**, and Kurdish is also an official language. The Kurdish regions in the north have their own government with extensive self-rule. The great majority of the population is Muslim, and many are Shia. The cities of **Najaf**, with the tomb of Imam Ali, and Karbala are important Shia places of pilgrimage.

Iraq has very large **oil reserves**. Selling oil brings the state the greatest part of its income. In the south lies the port city of **Basra**, through which a lot of oil is shipped. The access to the **Persian Gulf**, however, is only short. In recent decades the country has gone through several wars, which still makes rebuilding difficult today.

gewusst: Cuneiform writing from Mesopotamia is among the oldest scripts of humankind.
In the Bible the place Ur is named as Abraham’s place of origin.

teile.einleitung: **Japan** is an island state in East Asia, in the Pacific off the coast of China and Korea. The country combines very old traditions with the most modern technology. The capital city is **Tokyo**.
wichtigste: Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
The country’s name **Nihon** or **Nippon** means roughly “origin of the Sun”.
The flag is white with a red circle.
The money is called the **yen**.
In 2024 Japan had about 124 million inhabitants.
The express train **Shinkansen** has been running since 1964.

abschnitte.text: Seen from China, Japan lies in the east, where the Sun rises. That is why it is called the **Land of the Rising Sun**. The Japanese name **Nihon** or **Nippon** means roughly “origin of the Sun”. The flag also shows the Sun: a **red circle** on a white background. About 124 million people live in Japan (2024), many of them in big cities such as Tokyo and Osaka.

Well known is the Japanese food **sushi**: rice with vinegar, often with raw fish or vegetables. Many people eat with chopsticks. The art of folding paper into figures without scissors or glue is called **origami**. A popular subject is the crane. The tea ceremony, calligraphy and gardens also have a long tradition in Japan.

Every spring the **cherry trees** blossom in Japan. Then people celebrate **hanami**, the viewing of the blossom. Families and friends have picnics under the pink trees. On television it is even reported where the cherries are blossoming at the moment. The blossoms are seen as a sign of beauty that lasts only briefly.

**Sumo** is an old form of wrestling and a national sport of Japan. Two heavy wrestlers stand in a round ring. Whoever pushes the other out of the ring, or makes him touch the ground with any part of the body other than the soles of the feet, wins. Before the bout the wrestlers scatter salt, a custom from the Shinto religion.

Japan is known for cars, electronics and robots. Since 1964 the **Shinkansen** has been running, one of the first high-speed trains in the world. It is very fast and almost always on time. In Japan people pay with the **yen**.

gewusst: At 3,776 metres, Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan.
In Japan there are very many small earthquakes every year, which you often hardly feel.

teile.einleitung: The points of the compass help us to find our way around. There are four main points of the compass: north, east, south and west. In between lie other directions such as north-east or south-west.
wichtigste: There are four main points of the compass: north, east, south and west.
East lies opposite west, and north lies opposite south.
Between the main directions lie north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west.
They are abbreviated N, E, S and W, for example NW for north-west.
If you look north, you have east on your right and west on your left.
The memory aid “Never Eat Soggy Waffles” helps you to remember the order.
From Switzerland, Italy lies to the south and Austria to the east.

abschnitte.text: The four **main points of the compass** are **north**, **east**, **south** and **west**. Each two lie exactly opposite each other: north and south, east and west. In the east the Sun rises, and in the west it sets. At midday it stands in the south where we live. A **compass** needle always points north.

Between the main directions there are **intermediate points of the compass**. You form them by putting the names together. Between north and east lies **north-east**, and between south and west **south-west**. North or south always comes first. The directions are abbreviated with letters: N, E, S, W. North-west is therefore **NW**, and south-west **SW**.

A memory aid helps: **“Never Eat Soggy Waffles”**. The first letters N, E, S, W give the points of the compass **clockwise**. If you look north, east is on your **right**, west on your **left** and south behind you. On most maps north is at the top.

You can also describe Switzerland’s neighbouring countries using points of the compass. **Italy** lies to the **south**, behind the Alps. The canton of Ticino borders Italy. **Austria** lies to the **east** and borders the canton of the Grisons, for example. Germany lies to the north and France to the west.

gewusst: At night you can also find north without a compass: the Pole Star stands almost exactly in the north.
In German, east is “Osten”, which is why many German maps and compasses show an O instead of an E.

teile.einleitung: Havana is the capital of Cuba and lies on the north coast of the island. The city is known for its old town from the Spanish colonial period, for colourful vintage cars and for the long seafront promenade, the Malecón.
wichtigste: Havana is the capital and biggest city of Cuba.
The city lies on the north coast of the island.
The old town, Habana Vieja, with its fortresses, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
After 1959 hardly any new cars came into the country, which is why many old American cars are on the road.
The Malecón is a seafront promenade about 8 km long.

abschnitte.text: Havana was founded in the 16th century by the **Spanish**. The city was an important port, and strong **fortresses** protected it from attack. The old town is called **Habana Vieja**. It has narrow lanes, squares and houses from colonial times. Since **1982** it has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, together with its fortresses.

In Havana you see many **old American cars** from the **1950s**. After the revolution of **1959**, hardly any new cars came into the country. People therefore looked after and repaired their old cars again and again. Many of these colourful vintage cars are still on the road today and are also used as taxis for tourists.

The **Malecón** is the famous seafront road of Havana. It is about **8 kilometres** long and runs along the coast. In a storm the waves sometimes crash over the wall onto the road. In the evening many people meet there, sit on the wall, chat and listen to music.

Havana is known for its **music**. In many streets and bars you hear music such as **son** and **salsa**. The houses are often painted in bright colours, but many old buildings urgently need repairs. Havana is the political and cultural centre of Cuba.

gewusst: Some vintage cars in Havana run with engines or spare parts from completely different cars, because original parts are missing.

teile.einleitung: The **Jungfraujoch** is a mountain saddle between the peaks of the Mönch and the Jungfrau in the Bernese Alps. Here, at **3,454 m above sea level**, lies the highest railway station in Europe. You reach it by the Jungfrau Railway, which runs through a long tunnel inside the mountain.
wichtigste: The Jungfraujoch station lies at 3,454 m above sea level.
It is the highest railway station in Europe.
The **Jungfrau Railway** runs up from Kleine Scheidegg.
The railway was completed in 1912.
From the Joch you can see the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the biggest glacier in the Alps.

abschnitte.text: The **Jungfrau Railway** starts at **Kleine Scheidegg** and at first runs for a stretch in the open air. Then it disappears into a long **tunnel** that runs through the Eiger and the Mönch. On the way it stops at stations with windows in the rock face, for example at **Eismeer**. The idea came from the Zurich businessman **Adolf Guyer-Zeller**. After 16 years of construction the railway was opened in 1912.

Up on the Jungfraujoch there is a restaurant, viewing terraces and an **Ice Palace** in which figures made of ice stand. The **Sphinx** viewing platform lies a little higher still. In the Sphinx there is also a scientific station where researchers measure the air and the weather. Because of the thin air, you can easily feel dizzy up there.

abschnitte.titel: The Aletsch Glacier and World Heritage
abschnitte.text: From the Joch you look onto the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the longest glacier in the Alps. It flows south into Valais. The **Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch** region has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001. On the Joch runs the border between the cantons of **Bern** and **Valais**.

gewusst: Even in high summer there is snow on the Jungfraujoch.
The Jungfrau Railway is a rack railway, so that it can manage the steep sections.

teile.einleitung: Canada is the second biggest country in the world and lies in the north of North America. It is known for huge forests, lakes, maple syrup and ice hockey.
wichtigste: After Russia, Canada is the second biggest country on Earth.
It is about 240 times as big as Switzerland.
The official languages are English and French.
In the south Canada borders the USA.
Canada consists of ten provinces and three territories.
The biggest city is Toronto, and the capital city is Ottawa.

abschnitte.text: At just under **10 million km²**, Canada is, after Russia, the **second biggest country in the world**. It is about **240 times as big as Switzerland**. In the south Canada borders the **USA**. This border is the longest land border in the world between two countries. The north reaches far into the Arctic. Most people, though, live in the south, close to the border with the USA.

In Canada **English** and **French** are both official languages. Switzerland too has several official languages. In the province of **Quebec** people speak mainly French, and the city of **Montreal** lies there too. In the rest of the country English predominates. In addition, many Indigenous peoples live in Canada, such as the **Inuit** in the far north.

Canada is divided into **ten provinces** and **three territories**. Switzerland, by contrast, is divided into cantons. The **capital city** is **Ottawa**. The biggest city is **Toronto** on Lake Ontario. Other well-known cities are Montreal and Vancouver on the Pacific coast.

On Canada’s flag there is a red **maple leaf**. From the sap of maple trees **maple syrup** is boiled, and Canada produces the greatest part of it. The **beaver** has been an official symbol of the country since 1975 and is even shown on a coin. Since 1994 **ice hockey** has officially been the national winter sport.

Canada has huge **forests** and more lakes than almost any other country. In the **Rocky Mountains** in the west there are famous national parks. In the north lies the treeless **tundra**. There live polar bears, caribou and musk oxen. Also well known are **Niagara Falls** on the border with the USA.

gewusst: Canada has the longest coastline of all the countries in the world.
The greatest part of Canadian maple syrup comes from the province of Quebec.

teile.einleitung: The doldrums are a zone near the equator where there is often hardly any wind. For sailing ships this area was once feared, because they could be stuck there for days. In German it is called “Kalmen”.
wichtigste: The doldrums lie close to the equator.
There is often hardly any wind there.
The air there rises mainly straight upwards.
Sailing ships sometimes lay becalmed in the doldrums for days.
There are often clouds and heavy downpours there.

abschnitte.text: Sailors call the windless zone at the equator the **doldrums**. In German it is called “Kalmen”. For sailing ships it was a problem: without wind they could not move forward. Sometimes the ships lay stuck on the sea for **days**. The heat was great, and drinking water and supplies ran short.

abschnitte.titel: Why there is hardly any wind there
abschnitte.text: At the equator the Sun shines especially strongly. The air becomes warm and **rises**. From the north and south the **trade winds** flow in and meet here. Because the air rises mainly **vertically**, there is often only little wind near the ground. Experts speak of the **Intertropical Convergence Zone**.

The rising warm air cools at height. As it does so, tall **clouds** form. That is why in the doldrums there are often heavy **downpours** and thunderstorms, usually in the afternoon. In the course of the year the zone moves somewhat north and then south again, depending on where the Sun shines most strongly.

gewusst: In German the doldrums are also called “Mallungen”.
The heavy rain in this zone is the reason why the tropical rainforests around the equator grow so lushly.

teile.einleitung: A peninsula is a piece of land that sticks out into the water. It is surrounded by water on three sides and is joined to the rest of the land on only one side. There are huge peninsulas on which whole countries lie, and small ones in lakes.
wichtigste: A peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides.
Italy lies on a peninsula that looks like a boot.
Spain and Portugal lie on the Iberian Peninsula.
The Arabian Peninsula is the biggest peninsula in the world.
Norway and Sweden lie on the Scandinavian Peninsula.
Jutland belongs for the most part to Denmark.
The Au near Wädenswil is a peninsula in Lake Zurich.

abschnitte.text: An **island** is completely surrounded by water. A **peninsula**, by contrast, is surrounded by water on only three sides. On one side it is joined to the mainland. So it sticks out into the sea or into a lake. The German word says it already: it is, so to speak, half an island.

Europe has many big peninsulas. **Italy** sticks out into the Mediterranean and on the map looks like a boot. On the **Iberian Peninsula** in the south-west lie Spain and Portugal. Greece lies in the south of the **Balkan Peninsula**. In the north, Norway and Sweden share the **Scandinavian Peninsula**. **Jutland** sticks out north from Germany and belongs for the most part to Denmark.

The biggest peninsula in the world is the **Arabian Peninsula** in Asia. It lies between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. On it lie countries such as Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Oman. In North America **Florida** is well known: the state sticks far out into the sea in the south-east of the USA.

There are peninsulas in Swiss lakes too. One example is the **Au** near Wädenswil on Lake Zurich. It sticks out into the lake as a wooded hill. Not far from it lies the **Ufenau**. But this is not a peninsula, but a real island, because it is completely surrounded by water.

gewusst: The Arabian Peninsula is much bigger than Greenland, the biggest island in the world.
Some peninsulas are joined to the mainland only by a narrow strip of land. Such a strip is called an isthmus.

teile.einleitung: The **Inuit** are a people who have lived in the Arctic for a very long time, for example in Greenland, Canada and Alaska. They have learned to live in one of the coldest regions on Earth. Many things we know today, such as the kayak and the anorak, come from their culture.
wichtigste: The word “Inuit” means “people”.
In the past the Inuit lived mainly from hunting and fishing.
They made their warm clothes from animal skins.
Sled dogs pulled their sleds over ice and snow.
The kayak and the anorak are inventions from the Arctic.
In the east of Canada many Inuit speak the language **Inuktitut**.

abschnitte.text: The Inuit live in the far north: in **Greenland**, in the north of **Canada**, in **Alaska** and in the far east of Russia. There it is cold for many months, and in winter it stays dark for a long time. Hardly any trees grow. The word **Inuit** simply means “people” in their language. A single person is called an Inuk. In the past people often said “Eskimo”, but today the people’s own name, Inuit, is the usual one.

In the past the Inuit lived almost only on what the sea and land offered. They hunted seals, whales, caribou and polar bears and caught fish. Meat and fat provided food, skins kept them warm, and from bones they made tools. With the narrow, light **kayak** they hunted on the water. In winter **sled dogs** pulled their sleds over the ice.

The clothes of the Inuit were sewn from **animal skins** and kept them warm even in great cold. The hooded jacket that we call an **anorak** gets its name from an Inuit language. A special tool is the **ulu**, a half-moon-shaped knife traditionally used by women. With it you cut meat, skin and leather.

In the wide landscape the Inuit set up stone figures called **inuksuit**. They serve as signposts, mark good hunting places or show that people have been here. A single one is called an inuksuk. In the east of Canada many Inuit speak **Inuktitut**. Since 1999 there has been the territory of **Nunavut** in Canada, in which most people are Inuit.

Today most Inuit live in permanent houses in villages and towns. They drive snowmobiles and have schools and the internet. Many, however, hold on to old customs, still hunt, tell stories and look after their language. The igloo made of blocks of snow was built in the past mainly as shelter when hunting.

gewusst: The flag of the Canadian territory of Nunavut shows an inuksuk.
A well-built igloo can be much warmer inside than the icy air outside.

teile.einleitung: The Inca Trail is a famous hiking trail in the Andes of Peru. It follows old Inca paths and leads in several days to Machu Picchu. Because very many people want to walk it, the number of hikers is limited.
wichtigste: The Inca Trail is a hiking trail of several days to Machu Picchu.
It follows old Inca paths over high passes and past ruins.
The classic hike usually takes four days.
The number of hikers per day is limited.
The path ends at the Sun Gate above Machu Picchu.

abschnitte.text: The classic **Inca Trail** is about 40 kilometres long and usually takes **four days**. It leads over steep stone steps, through cloud forest and over high **passes**. The highest pass lies at over 4,000 metres. On the way you pass several Inca **ruins**. On the last morning you reach the **Sun Gate**, from which you look down on Machu Picchu.

In the 15th century the **Incas** built a huge **network of roads** through their empire in the Andes. It joined cities, villages and fortresses over many thousands of kilometres. Messengers ran along it carrying news from place to place. The Inca Trail is a small part of this network. The destination, **Machu Picchu**, is an Inca city high on a mountain ridge and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Because very many people want to walk the trail, the **number of hikers per day is limited**. You need a **permit** and have to go with an approved guide. Often the places are booked up months in advance. In this way the old path and nature are protected. For maintenance work the trail is closed every year in February.

gewusst: Many parts of the Inca Trail still consist today of the stone slabs that the Incas laid over 500 years ago.
The whole road network of the Incas, the Qhapaq Ñan, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.

teile.einleitung: **Jakarta** is the biggest city in Indonesia and lies on the north coast of the island of Java. The huge city struggles with a special problem: it is slowly sinking. It is also known for its national monument, **Monas**.
wichtigste: Jakarta lies on the **Java Sea** on the island of Java.
The city is sinking because a lot of groundwater is pumped out.
The national monument is called **Monas** and carries a golden flame at the top.
In the time of the Dutch the city was called Batavia.
Indonesia is building a new capital city on the island of Borneo.

abschnitte.text: Jakarta lies on the **Java Sea**, a shallow sea between the islands of Java and Borneo. Many rivers flow through the city into the sea. Many millions of people live in the region. In the rainy season there are often **floods**, because the water cannot drain away fast enough.

In Jakarta a great deal of **groundwater** is pumped out, because many houses have no connection to a water main. As a result the ground settles, and the city **sinks**. In some parts in the north it goes down by several centimetres a year. Some districts already lie below sea level. Large sea walls on the coast are meant to hold back the sea.

In the middle of the city stands **Monas**, the national monument of Indonesia. It is a tall, slender tower with a **golden flame** shining at its tip. It commemorates Indonesia’s struggle for independence. Visitors can go up in a lift and look out over the city.

In the time of Dutch colonial rule the city was called **Batavia** and was an important trading place. After independence Jakarta became the capital city of Indonesia. Because of the many problems, the government decided to build a new capital city called Nusantara on the island of **Borneo**.

gewusst: In the old town of Jakarta there are still buildings from the time of Batavia.
Jakarta is among the fastest sinking big cities in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Canadian Arctic Archipelago is a huge group of islands in the far north of Canada. It consists of tens of thousands of islands, most of them uninhabited and icy cold.
wichtigste: The archipelago consists of over 36,000 islands.
Together they are about 1.4 million km² in size.
The biggest island is Baffin Island, and the second biggest is Victoria Island.
The northernmost island of Canada is Ellesmere Island.
Iqaluit on Baffin Island is the capital of Nunavut.
The Franklin expedition was lost here from 1845.

abschnitte.text: The Canadian Arctic Archipelago lies north of the Canadian mainland. An **archipelago** is a group of islands. Here there are over **36,000 islands** with an area of about **1.4 million km²**. Only very few are inhabited. The islands belong to the territories of **Nunavut** and the **Northwest Territories**. Between them lie channels that are frozen over for a large part of the year.

**Baffin Island**, at about 507,000 km², is the biggest island in Canada and the fifth biggest in the world. The second biggest is **Victoria Island** at about 217,000 km², a good five times as big as Switzerland. Right in the north lies **Ellesmere Island**, close to Greenland. On it lies **Alert**, the northernmost permanently inhabited place in the world.

In this region live mainly **Inuit**. The biggest settlement is **Iqaluit** on Frobisher Bay in the south of Baffin Island. It is the **capital of Nunavut** and the only city in this territory. Many places can be reached only by aeroplane or, in summer, by ship.

For a long time navigators looked for a sea route from the Atlantic to the Pacific through the Arctic islands, the **Northwest Passage**. In 1845 **John Franklin** set out with 129 men and the ships **Erebus** and **Terror**. Nobody returned. Only in **2014** and **2016** were the wrecks of the two ships found.

On many islands lives the **musk ox**. With long outer hairs and dense underwool, it is well protected against the cold. Especially many live on **Banks Island** in the west. There are also polar bears, Arctic foxes and caribou. In the sea live seals, walruses and narwhals.

gewusst: Baffin Island is bigger than Germany, Austria and Switzerland put together.
In Alert on Ellesmere Island the Sun shines for months in summer, and in winter it stays dark for months.

teile.einleitung: Italy is a country in the south of Europe and lies to the south of Switzerland. On the map it looks like a long boot that juts out into the Mediterranean. The country is famous for its history, its art and its fine food.
wichtigste: Italy has the shape of a boot on the map.
The capital city of Italy is Rome.
About 59 million people live in Italy (as of 2024).
Pizza originally comes from Italy, more precisely from Naples.
In Venice you travel by boat on canals instead of by car.
Italy is a neighbour of Switzerland, and in Ticino people also speak Italian.
In the middle of Italy lie two small states of their own: Vatican City and San Marino.

abschnitte.text: Italy lies on the **Apennine Peninsula**, which reaches far into the Mediterranean. In the north the Alps form the border with Switzerland, France, Austria and Slovenia. The Apennine mountains run through the whole country. It also includes large islands such as **Sicily** and Sardinia. The longest river is the Po, which flows through the fertile Po Plain.

In Italy there are several active **volcanoes**. Etna on Sicily is the biggest active volcano in Europe. Vesuvius near Naples buried the Roman city of Pompeii under ash in the year AD 79. Because the African and Eurasian Plates meet here, there are also earthquakes again and again.

About 2,000 years ago Rome was the centre of the huge **Roman Empire**. In the 15th and 16th centuries the **Renaissance** began in cities such as Florence, a golden age of art and science with artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. For a long time Italy consisted of many small states. Only in 1861 did it become a single kingdom, and since 1946 it has been a republic.

Italian cooking is popular all over the world. Besides **pizza**, pasta, risotto, gelato and espresso are well known. In Italy people often eat several courses, for example pasta first and then meat or fish. Many dishes differ from region to region.

**Venice** is built on many small islands in a lagoon, and canals such as the Grand Canal run through the city. Instead of buses, water buses and the well-known gondolas run there. In Rome you can visit the **Colosseum**, a huge ancient arena. In Pisa stands the famous leaning tower, and Florence is known for its art museums.

Italian is one of the four national languages of Switzerland and is spoken mainly in Ticino and parts of the Grisons. Important links such as the Gotthard Base Tunnel lead from Switzerland to Italy. From the 1950s many people came from Italy to Switzerland as **workers**. To this day the Italian community is one of the biggest foreign groups in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A piece of land that is surrounded by water on three sides.
A shallow body of water by the sea that is separated from the open sea by islands or sandbanks.
A period in which the art and knowledge of antiquity were rediscovered.
A state without a king, whose head is elected.

gewusst: In Venice there are over 400 bridges, but almost no cars.
Vatican City, the smallest state in the world, lies in the middle of Rome.
The Margherita pizza is said to be named after an Italian queen.

teile.einleitung: **Isle Royale** is an island in **Lake Superior**, the biggest of the five Great Lakes in North America. It belongs to the US state of Michigan and is a national park. It is famous for a very long study of wolves and moose.
wichtigste: Isle Royale lies in Lake Superior and belongs to the USA.
The island is a national park with a lot of forest and few people.
Moose and wolves came to the island by themselves.
Since 1958 researchers have been studying here how wolves and moose live together.
It is the longest study of a predator and prey relationship in the world.

abschnitte.text: Isle Royale lies in the north-west of **Lake Superior**, close to the border with Canada. It is long and narrow and covered with forest. Since 1940 it has been a **national park**. There are no roads and no cars. Visitors come only by ship or seaplane and hike on trails or paddle canoes.

At the start of the 20th century **moose** came to the island, probably swimming. Later, in a very cold winter, **wolves** walked over the ice from the mainland. On the island the wolves hunt the moose. This created a small, closed system of predator and prey. Since 1958 researchers have counted and observed the two species every year.

The research shows that the numbers of wolves and moose go up and down. If there are many moose, the wolves find more food and become more numerous. Then the number of moose falls, and later that of the wolves too. When the wolves on the island had almost disappeared, new wolves were brought from the mainland from 2018 so that the balance is kept.

gewusst: The study on Isle Royale has been running for over 60 years.
