On the island there are lakes that themselves contain islands.

teile.einleitung: Guatemala is a country in Central America with volcanoes, lakes and rainforest. The Maya lived here, and many of their descendants still live there today. The national bird is the colourful quetzal.
wichtigste: The capital is called Guatemala City.
In the north and west Guatemala borders Mexico.
The Maya built the temple city of Tikal in the rainforest.
The national bird is the quetzal, and the currency is named after it too.
Lake Atitlán is surrounded by volcanoes.
The flag is light blue and white.

abschnitte.text: Guatemala lies in **Central America**. In the north and west it has a long border with **Mexico**. It also borders Belize, Honduras and El Salvador and lies on the Pacific and the Caribbean. The capital has almost the same name as the country: it is called **Guatemala City**. The official language is Spanish. The **flag** has two light blue stripes and a white stripe in the middle.

A long time ago the **Maya** already lived in Guatemala. They built big cities with temples and pyramids. The most famous is **Tikal** in the rainforest in the north of the country. It was one of the biggest cities of the Maya and flourished over 1000 years ago. Today the tall temples stand in the middle of the rainforest. Tikal is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

Many people in Guatemala are **descendants of the Maya**. Many still speak a Maya language today. Many Maya women wear **colourful, hand-woven** blouses and skirts. Often every village has its own patterns and colours. In the markets you can see and buy these fabrics.

In the highlands of Guatemala there are many **volcanoes**, and some are still active. **Lake Atitlán** lies in a huge old volcanic crater. Around it stand three volcanoes. On its shores lie many small Maya villages. Many people consider it one of the most beautiful lakes in the world.

The **quetzal** is the national bird of Guatemala. It has shimmering green and red feathers and a very long tail. It lives in damp mountain forests. The quetzal is shown on the **flag**. The country’s **currency** is also named after it and is called the quetzal.

gewusst: In Guatemala people pay with the quetzal, which is named after a bird.
In Guatemala more than twenty different Maya languages are spoken.

teile.einleitung: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam is a huge dam on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia. Its power station is the biggest hydroelectric power station in Africa. It is a source of pride for Ethiopia, but also causes disputes with its neighbours downstream.
wichtigste: The dam stands on the Blue Nile in the Benishangul-Gumuz region near the border with Sudan.
It was inaugurated in September 2025 after about 14 years of construction.
The power station has an output of about 5150 megawatts.
The reservoir holds about 74 billion cubic metres of water.
Filling began in July 2020.
Egypt and Sudan fear disadvantages for their water supply.

abschnitte.text: The **Blue Nile** rises from Lake Tana in the Ethiopian highlands. In Khartoum in Sudan it joins the White Nile to form the Nile. The dam stands in the west of Ethiopia, in the **Benishangul-Gumuz** region. It is only about 10 to 20 kilometres to the border with Sudan. Here the river flows from the highlands into the lowlands.

The power station has an installed output of about **5150 megawatts**. Originally 6000 megawatts were planned, but then the number of turbines was reduced to 13. This makes it the **biggest hydroelectric power station in Africa**. Many people in Ethiopia still have no electricity connection. The power station is meant to ease the shortage of electricity and also to supply electricity for export. The dam wall, at 145 metres, is not particularly high by comparison.

Construction work began in 2011. Ethiopia paid for the project **mainly from its own resources**. The state sold **bonds** to its citizens and collected contributions from government employees. For turbines and electrical equipment, loans from Chinese banks were added. In July 2020, during the rainy season, the first filling of the reservoir began. On 9 September 2025 the dam was officially inaugurated.

The reservoir can store about **74 billion cubic metres** of water. That is roughly one and a half times as much as the Blue Nile brings in a year. **Egypt** gets almost all of its water from the Nile, and **Sudan** also depends on the river. Both countries demand binding rules for filling and operating the dam, especially in drought years. Ethiopia, on the other hand, stresses its right to use the river for its own development. Several rounds of negotiations have so far brought no final agreement.

gewusst: Many people in Ethiopia contributed their own money to the building of the dam.
The name means roughly “dam of the great Ethiopian rebirth”.

teile.einleitung: The Valdés Peninsula lies on the Atlantic coast of Argentina in Patagonia. It is famous for its sea animals, above all for the whales in its bays. Since 1999 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The Valdés Peninsula lies in Patagonia in the south of Argentina.
It sticks out into the Atlantic Ocean.
In its sheltered bays southern right whales, a kind of whale, give birth to their young.
There you can also watch sea lions, elephant seals and penguins.
The peninsula has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

abschnitte.text: The **Valdés Peninsula** lies in the Argentine province of **Chubut** in Patagonia. It sticks out into the **Atlantic** and is joined to the mainland only by a narrow isthmus. The landscape is dry and flat, with grass and low bushes. Only a few people live there.

The peninsula is best known for the **southern right whales**. This is a large species of whale. Every year the whales come into the calm bays of the peninsula and give birth to their **young** there. You can watch them well from boats or from the shore. That is why the peninsula is an important destination for whale watching.

On the coasts there are also **sea lions**, **elephant seals** and **Magellanic penguins**. Sometimes **orcas** hunt young seals right on the beach. Because of this rich wildlife, the Valdés Peninsula was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list in **1999**. This is meant to keep the animals and their habitat protected.

gewusst: When hunting, the orcas off the Valdés Peninsula sometimes swim so far up the beach that they briefly stick half out of the water.

teile.einleitung: Greenland is the biggest island on Earth. Most of it is covered by a thick sheet of ice. The island belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark but manages many things itself.
wichtigste: Greenland is over 2 million square kilometres in size, more than 50 times as big as Switzerland.
About four fifths of the island are covered with ice.
Greenland belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.
The capital is called Nuuk.
Geographically, Greenland belongs to North America.
In 2025 only about 57,000 people lived in Greenland.

abschnitte.text: Greenland is over **2 million square kilometres** in size. Switzerland has about 41,000 square kilometres, so it would fit into Greenland over **50 times**. About **four fifths** of the island are covered by a thick **ice sheet**. Only on the coast is there ice-free land. The glaciers push their ice all the way into the sea. There, large pieces break off and drift away as **icebergs**.

In 2025 only about **57,000 people** lived in Greenland, fewer than in the city of Lucerne. Most live on the coast. Most are **Inuit**, and many speak **Greenlandic**. The capital **Nuuk** lies on the west coast and is the biggest town on the island. There are hardly any roads between the settlements, and people travel by ship, aeroplane or helicopter.

Greenland lies north-east of Canada. Geographically it therefore belongs to **North America**. Politically, however, it belongs to the **Kingdom of Denmark** in Europe. Greenland has its own government and its own parliament and manages many things itself. Denmark is responsible for foreign policy and defence, for example.

“Greenland” means **green land**. The Viking **Erik the Red** gave the island its name over a thousand years ago. With the pleasant name he wanted to attract settlers. The Vikings lived on the south-west coast for several centuries. Later their settlements disappeared again.

In the seas around Greenland lives the **narwhal**. In the male, one tooth grows into a long, twisted **tusk**. There are also polar bears, musk oxen, seals and whales. In summer in northern Greenland the Sun does not set, which is called the **midnight sun**. In winter, in return, it stays dark for weeks.

gewusst: Greenland is the biggest island on Earth that is not a continent.
Although the island is huge, fewer people live there than in Lucerne.

teile.einleitung: The Grande Dixence is a gigantic dam in the canton of Valais. At 285 metres it is the highest gravity dam in the world. It holds back the Lac des Dix and supplies water for large power stations.
wichtigste: The dam stands at the very end of the Val des Dix in Valais.
It is 285 metres high and so the highest gravity dam in the world.
A gravity dam holds back the water through its enormous weight alone.
Behind the dam lies the reservoir Lac des Dix.
It was built in the 1950s.

abschnitte.text: There are different kinds of dams. An **arch dam** is curved and passes the pressure of the water on to the rock walls. A **gravity dam**, on the other hand, is very thick at the bottom and holds back the water through its **enormous weight** alone. The Grande Dixence is such a dam. It is **285 metres** high, taller than any church tower and almost as tall as the Eiffel Tower. Building it took millions of cubic metres of concrete.

Behind the dam lies the reservoir **Lac des Dix**. It is filled by meltwater from the glaciers. Through long **tunnels** in the mountain, extra water is brought in from other Valais valleys, even from the area around Zermatt. In summer the lake fills up, and in winter the water is used when more electricity is needed. In power stations further down it drives turbines.

The dam was built in the **1950s** and finished around 1961. It lies in the municipality of Hérémence. In summer you can drive up to the dam and walk along its crest. A cable car leads up to the lake. Inside the dam there are passages that you can see on guided tours.

gewusst: The Grande Dixence is one of the biggest structures in Switzerland.
Hydropower supplies the largest part of the electricity in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Africa has over 50 states and therefore over 50 capitals. Some are old cities on the coast, others were newly planned in the interior. Some countries even have several capitals.
wichtigste: Abuja has been the capital of Nigeria since 1991.
In Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, the African Union has its seat.
South Africa has three capitals, and Pretoria is the seat of government.
Kinshasa and Brazzaville face each other across the Congo River.
Rabat is the capital of Morocco, and Casablanca is the biggest city.
Dodoma is the official capital of Tanzania.
Accra is the capital of Ghana.

abschnitte.text: Some African countries have moved their capital to the interior. **Abuja** was newly planned in the middle of **Nigeria** and has been the capital since **1991**. Before that, Lagos on the coast was the capital. In **Tanzania**, **Dodoma** in the interior is the official capital. The port city of **Dar es Salaam**, however, is much bigger and economically more important.

**Addis Ababa** is the capital of **Ethiopia**. It lies high in the highlands at about 2350 metres above sea level. The **African Union** has its headquarters there. In it, almost all the states of Africa work together. That is why Addis Ababa is sometimes also called the political capital of Africa.

**South Africa** has no fewer than three capitals. In **Pretoria** the government sits. In **Cape Town** the parliament meets. In **Bloemfontein** the highest court has its seat. In this way the tasks are spread across different parts of the country.

abschnitte.titel: On the river and on the coast
abschnitte.text: **Kinshasa** is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It lies on the **Congo River**, directly opposite **Brazzaville**, the capital of the Republic of the Congo. Kinshasa is a huge city with many millions of inhabitants. **Rabat** in **Morocco** lies on the Atlantic coast and is the seat of the king and the government, while **Casablanca** is bigger. **Accra**, the capital of **Ghana**, lies on the Gulf of Guinea.

gewusst: Kinshasa and Brazzaville are the two capitals in the world that lie closest together, if you do not count Rome and Vatican City.
Addis Ababa means “new flower” in Amharic.

teile.einleitung: Cacti are plants that are perfectly adapted to dry regions. They store water in their thick bodies and protect themselves with spines.
wichtigste: Cacti store water in their thick, fleshy stem.
Their spines are modified leaves.
The spines protect against animals and save water.
Almost all cacti come from the Americas.
Many cacti have flat, wide-spreading roots.
Some cacti flower for only a single night.

abschnitte.text: In deserts it rarely rains. A cactus therefore has a thick, **fleshy stem**. In it it stores a lot of **water** for long, dry periods. Many cacti have ribs. When they soak up water, these expand like an accordion. Because the cactus has hardly any leaves, the green stem is also the part that makes food using sunlight.

The **spines** of a cactus are **modified leaves**. Through large leaves a lot of water would evaporate, but through thin spines hardly any. The spines have a second job as well: they **protect** the juicy cactus from thirsty and hungry animals. In addition, many spines give a little shade. A thick skin with a **layer of wax** also keeps the water inside.

Many cacti have **shallow roots** that spread far around the plant. When it does rain, they take up the water quickly, before it soaks away or evaporates. Other cacti also have a deep main root. In this way they survive long dry periods too.

Cacti grow naturally almost only in **North and South America**. They came to Africa, Europe and Australia only with people. In the Arizona desert grows the giant **saguaro** with its arms. It can grow over 12 metres tall and over 150 years old. But it grows very slowly.

Many cacti have large, colourful **flowers**. They shine red, yellow, pink or white. Some cacti flower for only **a single night**. Their flowers are then visited by moths or bats. Cacti are also popular as house plants, because they need little care.

gewusst: A large saguaro can take up a great deal of water after rain and become clearly heavier as a result.
The fruits of some cacti can be eaten, for example the prickly pear.

teile.einleitung: The Kalahari is a large dry region in southern Africa. Although it is called a desert, grass, bushes and trees grow there, and many animals live in it.
wichtigste: The Kalahari lies in southern Africa.
A large part of Botswana is Kalahari, and it also reaches into Namibia and South Africa.
Its sand is often coloured red.
More rain falls than in the Sahara, so grass and bushes grow.
The San have lived in the Kalahari for a very long time.
Meerkats, lions and sociable weavers live there.

abschnitte.text: The Kalahari lies in **southern Africa**. A large part of **Botswana** belongs to it, but it also reaches into **Namibia** and **South Africa**. In many areas the sand is coloured **red**, and the dunes glow especially in the evening. In the Kalahari somewhat more rain falls than in the Sahara. That is why **grass**, **bushes** and a few trees such as acacias grow there. People therefore also speak of a dry savanna.

Well known are the **meerkats**. They live in groups, and one often stands upright on its hind legs and keeps **watch**. **Lions** also hunt in the Kalahari. They can go a long time without drinking and also get liquid from their prey. The **sociable weavers** build huge communal nests from grass with many chambers. Inside it stays cool by day and warm at night.

The **San** are among the oldest peoples of Africa. They have lived in the Kalahari for a very long time and know the desert very well. In the past they lived as **hunters and gatherers**. They knew where to find water and which plants are edible. Their languages are known for special **click sounds**.

In the middle of the Kalahari in Botswana lies the **Central Kalahari Game Reserve**. It is one of the biggest protected areas in the world and even bigger than Switzerland. In the north-east of Botswana lie the **Makgadikgadi Pans**. They are the remains of a large lake that dried up long ago. Today they are among the biggest salt flats on Earth.

gewusst: A single nest of sociable weavers can become so heavy that whole branches break under it.
On the northern edge of the Kalahari the Okavango River seeps away in a huge inland delta, instead of flowing into the sea.

t9zta78.t: Border between Mexico and the United States

teile.einleitung: The border between Mexico and the United States is about 3100 kilometres long. It runs from the Pacific to the Gulf of Mexico. It is one of the most crossed borders in the world.
wichtigste: The border is about 3145 kilometres long.
For about 2000 kilometres the Rio Grande forms the border.
The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo of 1848 laid the basis for today’s course.
With the Gadsden Purchase in 1853 the border essentially took its present form.
San Ysidro between San Diego and Tijuana is one of the busiest land border crossings in the world.
Every year there are about 350 million legal border crossings.

abschnitte.titel: From the Pacific to the Gulf
abschnitte.text: The border is about **3145 kilometres** long. It begins at the **Pacific** between San Diego and Tijuana and ends at the **Gulf of Mexico**. On the way it crosses deserts, mountains and river valleys. For about 2000 kilometres the **Rio Grande** forms the border, and in Mexico it is called the Río Bravo del Norte. It separates Texas from Mexico. Further west, the border is mostly a straight line through the land.

From 1846 to 1848 Mexico and the USA fought a war against each other. In the **Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo** of 1848, Mexico gave up large areas, including California and parts of New Mexico. The Rio Grande was recognised as the border with Texas. In 1853 the USA bought a further area in the south of what is now Arizona and New Mexico through the **Gadsden Purchase**. It was meant to make it easier to build a railway to California. Since then the border has essentially followed its present course.

Along the border lie many pairs of cities. **El Paso** in Texas lies directly opposite **Ciudad Juárez**. Together they form a large urban area. Between **San Diego** and **Tijuana** lies the crossing of **San Ysidro**. About 50,000 vehicles pass through there every day, and many pedestrians too. Many people commute across for work, school or shopping.

From 1942 to 1964 the USA recruited Mexican workers through the **Bracero Program**, mainly for farming. It began because of the shortage of workers in the Second World War. Today there are many **maquiladoras** in the Mexican border area. These are assembly plants that import parts duty-free, put them together and deliver the products to the USA. With about **350 million** legal crossings a year, the border is very busy.

Many people try to get into the USA without permission. That is why **fences** and walls have been built along many sections, and the border is closely watched. How to deal with immigration is very controversial politically in the USA. Some demand more protection and checks, while others campaign for more legal routes and for the rights of migrants.

gewusst: A large part of the present-day western USA belonged to Mexico until 1848.
The Rio Grande has two names: in Mexico it is called the Río Bravo del Norte.

teile.einleitung: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It runs deep under the Gotthard massif from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to Bodio in Ticino.
wichtigste: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long.
It is the longest railway tunnel in the world and was opened in 2016.
Its highest point is only about 550 metres above sea level.
With the Ceneri Base Tunnel, the Gotthard route has been a flat railway since 2020.
The Alpine Initiative of 1994 demands that transit freight traffic be moved onto the railways.
A second road tube is being built at the Gotthard so that the old tunnel can be renovated.

abschnitte.text: The **Gotthard Base Tunnel** is about **57 kilometres** long and so the **longest railway tunnel in the world**. It runs from **Erstfeld** in the canton of Uri to **Bodio** in Ticino. The tunnel consists of two tubes, each with one track. It was built as part of **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps. After many years of construction it was opened in June 2016.

abschnitte.titel: A flat railway through the Alps
abschnitte.text: A **base tunnel** lies deep at the foot of the mountains instead of high up. The highest point of the Gotthard Base Tunnel is only about **550 metres above sea level**, barely higher than the Central Plateau. That is why long, heavy **freight trains** can run without extra locomotives, and passenger trains are faster. Since 2020 the **Ceneri Base Tunnel** in Ticino, about 15 kilometres long, has completed the route. Since then the Gotthard route between Uri and Lugano has been a continuous **flat railway**.

A great many lorries drive through the Alps. In 1994 the people and the cantons accepted the **Alpine Initiative**. It demands that freight traffic across the Alps be moved from the road to the **railways**. This task has been in the **Federal Constitution** ever since. The Gotthard Base Tunnel is an important means of reaching this goal.

Besides the railway tunnel there is the **Gotthard Road Tunnel** of 1980. It has to be extensively renovated. So that it does not have to be closed completely for years for this, a **second tube** is being built. The voters approved this construction in 2016. When both tubes are finished, each is supposed to have only one lane, because by law the capacity must not increase.

When building the base tunnel, the workers had to drill through hard rock deep under the mountains. In some places there are over 2000 metres of rock above the tunnel. It is very hot inside the mountain there, so the tunnel had to be cooled heavily. Huge **tunnel boring machines** cut their way through the rock. The breakthrough took place in 2010, when the construction teams met inside the mountain.

gewusst: In the Gotthard Base Tunnel the rock could get hotter than 40 degrees without cooling.
The first Gotthard railway tunnel, higher up in the mountain, was already opened in 1882.

teile.einleitung: **James Cook** was a British navigator and explorer of the 18th century. He led three great voyages into the Pacific and drew very exact maps. Europeans got to know many coasts, islands and seas only through him.
wichtigste: James Cook came from Britain.
On his first voyage from 1768 he sailed with the **Endeavour**.
In 1770 he was the first European to chart the **east coast of Australia**.
He led three great voyages of discovery into the Pacific.
With **sauerkraut** he protected his crew from scurvy.
In 1779 he died in Hawaii.

abschnitte.titel: From a farm worker’s son to captain
abschnitte.text: James Cook was born in 1728 in northern England. His father was a farm labourer. As a young man he learned seafaring on coal ships. Later he joined the British navy and became known because he could survey and **chart** coasts very precisely. That is why he was given command of a great voyage of exploration.

From 1768 Cook sailed with the ship **Endeavour** into the Pacific. First he observed on Tahiti a rare transit of Venus across the Sun. After that he sailed around New Zealand and charted it. In 1770 he reached the **east coast of Australia** and landed in **Botany Bay**, near present-day Sydney. He was the first European to explore this coast.

In all Cook led **three** great voyages into the Pacific. On the second voyage he looked for a great southern continent. In doing so, in 1773 he was the first known navigator to cross the **Antarctic Circle**. He did not see Antarctica itself, because the ice stopped him. On the third voyage he looked for a sea route north around America.

On long sea voyages many sailors got **scurvy**, a dangerous illness caused by a lack of vitamin C. Cook took **sauerkraut** along, among other things, and made sure of fresh food and cleanliness. In this way he lost far fewer men to this illness than other captains of his time.

In 1779 a quarrel broke out in **Hawaii** between Cook’s men and local people. In it Cook was killed. Today his voyages are also viewed critically: they paved the way for colonisation, which brought great suffering to the original inhabitants of Australia, New Zealand and Hawaii.

gewusst: Many places bear Cook’s name, for example the Cook Islands and Cook Strait in New Zealand.
The highest mountain in New Zealand is called Mount Cook in English.

teile.einleitung: Henequen is a kind of agave whose leaves yield strong fibres. Around 1900 this plant made the Mexican Yucatán Peninsula rich, because ropes and twine were made from the fibres.
wichtigste: Henequen is an agave whose leaves yield strong fibres.
Ship’s ropes and binding twine were made from the fibres.
Around 1900 henequen brought great wealth to the Yucatán Peninsula.
The plantation owners became rich, while the Maya workers often lived in debt bondage.
When artificial fibres came along, henequen became less important.

abschnitte.text: **Henequen** is an **agave**. It has long, thick, spiky leaves that form a rosette. The plant copes well with little water and the stony limestone soil of Yucatán. From its leaves, strong **fibres** are obtained, similar to sisal. These fibres are very tear-resistant.

Around **1900**, huge henequen plantations were laid out on Yucatán. From the fibres, **ship’s ropes** and **binding twine** were made, with which farmers tied up sheaves of grain, for example. Demand, especially from the USA, was great. The plantation owners became very rich. In the city of **Mérida** they built magnificent villas. Henequen was therefore called **“green gold”**.

The hard work on the plantations was done mainly by **Maya**. Many of them lived in **debt bondage**: they owed money to the plantation owner and so were not allowed to leave. Later **artificial fibres** came along, and henequen was needed less. Many old plantation estates, the haciendas, now stand empty or are hotels and museums.

gewusst: Many henequen plantations had their own small railways to bring the leaves to be processed.

teile.einleitung: An igloo is a house made of snow in the shape of a dome. The Inuit in the Arctic built igloos mainly as shelter when hunting. Although it is made of snow, it is much warmer inside than outside.
wichtigste: An igloo is built from firm blocks of snow.
It has the shape of a dome, like half a ball.
Snow contains a lot of air and therefore keeps the warmth inside.
The Inuit often used igloos as shelter on long hunting trips.
The entrance is low and like a tunnel, so that cold air stays outside.
The blocks were cut with a long snow knife.

abschnitte.text: For an igloo you cut **blocks** out of firm, packed snow. The Inuit used a long **snow knife** made of bone for this, and later of metal. The blocks are laid in a circle and built upwards in a spiral. They lean further and further inwards until a **dome** forms. At the very top a keystone is put in.

A great deal of **air** is trapped in snow. Air conducts heat poorly, so snow is a good **insulator**. The body heat of the people and a small **oil lamp** are enough to make it much warmer inside than outside. Outside it can be icy cold, and inside the temperature is often around freezing point or above.

The entrance of an igloo is often **low** and **like a tunnel**. Cold air is heavy and stays down. That is why it does not flow into the higher living space. The warm air collects at the top of the dome. Often the sleeping area is raised, so that you lie in the warmth.

The **Inuit** live in the Arctic, for example in Canada and Greenland. Many built igloos as **shelter when hunting** in winter. An experienced builder could do it in a few hours. At other times they often lived in houses made of stone, earth or fur. The word “igloo” simply means “house” in their language.

gewusst: An igloo is so stable that a person can climb onto the finished dome.
In the Swiss Alps too there are igloo villages in winter where you can spend the night.

teile.einleitung: A hot day is a day on which the temperature reaches at least 30 degrees. MeteoSwiss counts such days to show how hot a summer was. Hot days can be tiring for people, animals and plants.
wichtigste: A hot day has a maximum temperature of at least 30 °C.
From 25 °C people speak of a summer day.
If the temperature does not fall below 20 °C at night, it is a tropical night.
In Switzerland there are hot days mainly in Ticino, Geneva, Basel and Valais.
Because of global warming, Switzerland has more hot days than in the past.

abschnitte.text: Weather services such as **MeteoSwiss** have exact names for warm days. If the maximum temperature reaches **25 °C** or more, it is called a **summer day**. If it rises to **30 °C** or more, it is a **hot day**. If it stays above **20 °C** at night, that is called a **tropical night**. Measurements are always taken in the shade, about two metres above the ground.

In Switzerland there are hot days mainly at low altitudes, for example in **Ticino**, **Geneva**, **Basel** and **Valais**. In the mountains it is usually cooler, because the temperature falls with height. The highest temperature ever measured in Switzerland was **41.5 °C** in **Grono** in the canton of the Grisons in the summer of 2003. Because of **global warming** there are more hot days today than in the past.

On hot days it is important to drink a lot of **water**. It is best to stay in the **shade** or indoors at midday. Light, pale clothes and a hat help. Especially older people, small children and the sick need protection. In great heat MeteoSwiss issues **heat warnings**.

gewusst: An ice day is the opposite of a hot day: on an ice day the temperature does not rise above 0 °C all day.

teile.einleitung: Grenada is a small island state in the Caribbean. Because of its many spices it is called the “Spice Island”. A nutmeg is even shown on its flag.
wichtigste: Grenada lies in the south of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean.
The capital is called St George’s.
The smaller islands of Carriacou and Petite Martinique also belong to the state.
Grenada is one of the biggest producers of nutmeg.
The flag shows a nutmeg.

abschnitte.text: Grenada lies in the south of the **Lesser Antilles**, not far from Venezuela. The state includes the main island of Grenada and the smaller islands of **Carriacou** and **Petite Martinique**. The capital is **St George’s**, with a beautiful natural harbour. The island is volcanic in origin, mountainous and green. Grenada used to be a British colony and has been independent since **1974**. The official language is English.

Many spices grow on Grenada, for example **nutmeg**, cinnamon, cloves and ginger. That is why it is called the **Spice Island**. Grenada is one of the biggest producers of nutmeg in the world. That is why a nutmeg is shown on the **flag**. The flag is red, yellow and green and has seven stars. Besides spices, cocoa and tourism are important.

Like other Caribbean islands, Grenada is sometimes hit by **hurricanes**. In 2004 Hurricane Ivan caused great damage. Many houses and also many nutmeg trees were destroyed. It took years for the trees to grow back.

gewusst: Grenada is one of the few countries with a spice on its flag.

teile.einleitung: Chocolate is made from cocoa. The beans grow on the cocoa tree in warm countries, and Switzerland has made famous chocolate from them, although no cocoa grows here.
wichtigste: The cocoa tree comes from the Americas.
Its fruits grow directly on the trunk and are often called cocoa pods.
Raw cocoa beans taste very bitter.
Ivory Coast harvests the most cocoa, and Ghana is also very important.
The Maya were already drinking cocoa.
Daniel Peter from Vevey invented milk chocolate.

abschnitte.text: The cocoa tree needs warmth, moisture and shade. It grows in the tropics. Unusually, its fruits hang **directly on the trunk** and on thick branches. The oblong fruit is often called a **cocoa pod**. Inside it lie many **cocoa beans** in white, sweetish pulp. Raw, the beans taste very **bitter**.

The cocoa tree comes from the **Americas**. The **Maya** in Central America made a bitter drink from cocoa long ago, often with spices. The Aztecs also valued cocoa greatly and even used the beans as money. After the arrival of the Europeans, cocoa came to Spain and later became fashionable all over Europe, now sweetened with sugar.

Today most cocoa comes from **West Africa**. **Ivory Coast** harvests more than any other country, almost half of the world’s cocoa beans (as of 2024). **Ghana** on the Gulf of Guinea is also among the most important cocoa countries. There **Tetteh Quarshie** is regarded as the founder of cocoa growing. According to tradition, he brought cocoa seeds to the then Gold Coast at the end of the 19th century.

After the harvest the beans are **fermented** for a few days, and then dried. In the factory they are roasted and ground. From this you get **cocoa powder** and the pale fat **cocoa butter**. **White chocolate** contains only cocoa butter and no brown cocoa powder. With sugar and often milk, chocolate is made from it.

In Switzerland it is far too cold for cocoa trees. The beans are **imported** and processed here. In the 19th century **Daniel Peter** from **Vevey** invented **milk chocolate**. Soon afterwards **Rodolphe Lindt** in Bern developed a process that makes chocolate melt especially smoothly. Since then Swiss chocolate has been known all over the world.

gewusst: The scientific name of the cocoa tree, Theobroma, means “food of the gods”.
A cocoa tree bears flowers and fruits directly on the trunk, often at the same time.

teile.einleitung: The **Yenisei** is a huge river in **Siberia**, in the Asian part of Russia. It flows from south to north into the Arctic Ocean. No other river in Russia carries so much water.
wichtigste: The Yenisei is considered the river with the most water in Russia.
It flows into the **Kara Sea**, a part of the Arctic Ocean.
It roughly separates **Western Siberia** and **Eastern Siberia**.
The city of **Krasnoyarsk**, with over a million people, lies on the Yenisei.
Its power is used with large **hydroelectric power stations** to generate electricity.

abschnitte.text: The Yenisei begins in the mountains in the south of Siberia, near the border with Mongolia. From there it flows over thousands of kilometres to the **north**. An important tributary is the **Angara**, which comes from Lake Baikal. At the end the Yenisei flows into the **Kara Sea** in a broad bay. In winter the river is frozen for many months.

The Yenisei divides Siberia roughly into two parts. To the west lies the flat **West Siberian Plain** with many swamps. To the east the land rises to the **Central Siberian Plateau**. That is why the two banks are often very different: one flat, the other high and steep.

On the Yenisei stand large **hydroelectric power stations** that generate a lot of electricity. One of them is the Krasnoyarsk hydroelectric power station. The biggest power station in Russia, the Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric power station, also dams the Yenisei. The electricity is used, among other things, to run large aluminium plants.

The biggest city on the Yenisei is **Krasnoyarsk**, a Siberian city of over a million people. Far in the north, beyond the Arctic Circle, lies the port of **Dudinka**. Through it the industrial city of **Norilsk** is connected to the world, because no road leads to it from the south. In summer ships travel up and down the river.

gewusst: If you include the source river Selenga and the Angara, the river system of the Yenisei is over 5,000 kilometres long.
Together with the Ob and the Lena, the Yenisei is one of the three great rivers of Siberia.

teile.einleitung: **Jerusalem** is one of the oldest cities in the world. It is holy to three religions: **Judaism**, **Christianity** and **Islam**. That is why pilgrims from all over the world come to the city every year.
wichtigste: Jerusalem is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims.
The **Old City** is surrounded by a wall and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Western Wall is the most important place of prayer in Judaism.
Christians revere the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, where Jesus is said to have been buried.
On the Temple Mount stand the Dome of the Rock and the Al-Aqsa Mosque.
The status of the city is politically disputed.

abschnitte.text: For Jews, Jerusalem is the holiest city. Here once stood the **Temple**. Part of its surrounding wall is preserved, the **Western Wall**, also called the Wailing Wall. Many people pray there and push small slips of paper with wishes and prayers into the cracks between the stones.

For Christians, Jerusalem is the place where Jesus is said to have died and risen. The **Church of the Holy Sepulchre** stands on the spot where, according to tradition, his tomb was. Many pilgrims walk the **Via Dolorosa**, which recalls the path of suffering of Jesus.

For Muslims, Jerusalem is the third holiest city after Mecca and Medina. On the **Temple Mount**, in Arabic Haram al-Sharif, stands the **Dome of the Rock** with its golden dome. Next to it stands the **Al-Aqsa Mosque**. According to Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad travelled from here up to heaven.

The Old City is divided into four quarters: the Jewish, the Christian, the Muslim and the Armenian. Israel regards Jerusalem as its capital city. The Palestinians see the eastern part as the capital of a future state of their own. Many countries are waiting for an agreement, and so the status of the city is internationally **disputed**.

gewusst: The Old City of Jerusalem is smaller than one square kilometre.
The present wall of the Old City was built in the 16th century under the Ottomans.

teile.einleitung: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt and one of the biggest cities in Africa. It lies on the Nile, where the Nile Delta begins, and is over a thousand years old.
wichtigste: Cairo is the capital city and biggest city of Egypt.
Over 20 million people live in the city and its surroundings.
The Fatimids founded Cairo in the year 969.
The city lies at the tip of the Nile Delta.
The people speak Arabic.
Right next to Cairo lies Giza with the pyramids.

abschnitte.titel: A giant city on the Nile
abschnitte.text: Cairo is the **capital city** of Egypt. Together with the suburbs, over 20 million people live here. The city lies on the **Nile**, shortly before the river divides into many arms and forms the **Nile Delta**. This location made Cairo an important hub for trade and transport. In the west Cairo has grown together with the city of **Giza**, where the famous pyramids stand.

Cairo was founded in the year **969** by the **Fatimids**, a Muslim ruling family. They called the new capital city **al-Qahira**, which means “the Victorious”. From this came the name Cairo. Nearby, though, there had been settlements much earlier, such as the old capital city of Memphis. Today the old town of Cairo is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

A **minaret** is the tower of a mosque. Cairo has so many of them that it is called the **“City of a Thousand Minarets”**. In the city also stands **Al-Azhar**, a mosque with a university. It is over 1,000 years old and is among the oldest universities in the world. Most people in Cairo are Muslims, but there are also Christian Copts.

In Cairo people speak **Arabic**, the official language of Egypt. In the old town lies the big bazaar **Khan el-Khalili**. There you can buy spices, lamps, cloths and jewellery. Traffic in the city is often dense and noisy. Since **1987** an **underground railway**, the Metro, has been running. It was the first underground railway in Africa.

In the middle of Cairo lies **Tahrir Square**. In **2011** hundreds of thousands of people gathered there and demanded political change. After 18 days of protest, President **Hosni Mubarak** stepped down. At the edge of the square stood for a long time the Egyptian Museum with many treasures of the pharaohs.

gewusst: Cairo is one of the biggest cities in Africa.
The name al-Qahira means “the Victorious”.

teile.einleitung: A halocline is a layer in water where the salt content suddenly changes sharply. It is particularly easy to see in the caves and cenotes of Yucatán, where fresh water lies on top of salt water.
wichtigste: The halocline is the boundary between water with little salt and water with a lot of salt.
Salt water is heavier than fresh water and therefore lies at the bottom.
In the cenotes of Yucatán, fresh water floats on seawater that has seeped in.
At the halocline, divers see a shimmer like the heat over a road.
Haloclines also exist in seas, for example in the Baltic Sea.

abschnitte.text: The word **halocline** comes from Greek: “hals” means salt, “klinein” means to slope. It means a layer in water in which the **salt content** changes sharply over a short distance. **Salt water** is heavier than **fresh water**. If the two do not mix, the lighter fresh water lies on top and the heavier salt water at the bottom.

On the Yucatán Peninsula, rain seeps into the limestone and collects underground as fresh water. From the coast, **seawater** flows into the caves. The fresh water floats on top of it. Divers in the **cenotes** pass from fresh water into salt water at a certain depth. At this boundary the water **shimmers**, similar to hot air over a road. Visibility becomes briefly blurred there.

Haloclines do not exist only in caves. Such layers also form in seas into which a lot of river water flows. One example is the **Baltic Sea**. There, water with less salt lies over deep water with more salt. The layer can stop the water at the top and bottom from mixing well.

gewusst: The shimmer at the halocline occurs because light is bent by different amounts in salt water and in fresh water.

teile.einleitung: The **Itaipú Dam** is one of the biggest hydroelectric power stations in the world. It dams the **Paraná** River on the border between Brazil and Paraguay. The two countries run the power station together.
wichtigste: Itaipú lies on the Paraná River.
Brazil and Paraguay run the power station together.
The installed capacity is **14,000 megawatts**.
Ten generators each run at 50 and at 60 hertz.
Paraguay sells the greatest part of its electricity to Brazil.
In 1982 the reservoir flooded the Guaíra Falls.

abschnitte.text: The Itaipú power station has 20 large **generators** and an installed capacity of **14,000 megawatts**. It was built in the 1970s and 1980s. For a long time it produced more electricity per year than any other power station. In 2020 the **Three Gorges Dam** in China set a new record and replaced Itaipú as record holder.

Electricity flows as alternating current, which reverses direction many times a second. This is called the **frequency** and is measured in hertz. Paraguay uses 50 hertz like Switzerland, but Brazil uses 60 hertz. That is why in Itaipú ten generators run at 50 hertz and ten at 60 hertz. Paraguay needs only a small part of its share and **sells** the greatest part to Brazil.

Behind the wall a large **reservoir** builds up. When it was filled in 1982, the mighty **Guaíra Falls**, also called Sete Quedas, disappeared for ever under water. For many people this was a great loss. The name **Itaipú** comes from the Guaraní language and means roughly “singing stone”.

The dam lies close to the border towns of **Foz do Iguaçu** in Brazil and **Ciudad del Este** in Paraguay. Not far away, the famous Iguazú Falls plunge down. Many tourists visit both: the nature of the waterfalls and the huge structure of Itaipú.

gewusst: Itaipú covers a very large part of Paraguay’s electricity needs.
The dam wall of Itaipú is several kilometres long.

teile.einleitung: Hawaii is a US state in the middle of the Pacific. It consists of many islands that were formed from volcanoes. Hawaii used to be a kingdom of its own and is the home of surfing.
wichtigste: In 1959 Hawaii became the 50th and so far last state of the USA.
The capital is Honolulu on the island of Oʻahu.
Hawaii has eight main islands and many small islands.
The biggest island is also called Hawaii and is often called the “Big Island”.
Surfing has its roots in Hawaii.
A lei is a garland of flowers given as a greeting.
Kamehameha I united the islands into one kingdom by 1810.

abschnitte.text: Hawaii lies in the middle of the **Pacific Ocean**, far away from any mainland. There are **eight main islands**, including Hawaii, Maui, **Oʻahu** and Kauaʻi, as well as many small islands and atolls. The biggest island has the same name as the whole state: **Hawaii**. So that it is not mixed up, it is often called the **“Big Island”**.

In the past there were several rulers on the islands. **Kamehameha I** united the islands by **1810** into the **Kingdom of Hawaii**. This kingdom lasted until **1893**. After that Hawaii came under the influence of the USA. In August **1959** Hawaii was admitted as the **50th state**. Since then the flag of the USA has had 50 stars.

The capital **Honolulu** lies on the island of **Oʻahu**. It is the biggest city in Hawaii. There lies the well-known beach of **Waikīkī**, where many tourists swim and surf. Nearby is also the harbour of **Pearl Harbor**.

People in Hawaii were already riding the waves on boards centuries ago. From there **surfing** spread all over the world. Also well known is the **lei**: a garland of flowers, leaves or shells. It is hung around guests’ necks as a greeting. A lei is a sign of **friendship** and **welcome**.

gewusst: The Hawaiian alphabet has only 13 letters.
The word “aloha” means both hello and goodbye in Hawaiian and expresses affection.

teile.einleitung: **Jamaica** is an island in the Caribbean, south of Cuba. The country is world famous for its music, **reggae**, and for very fast runners. The capital city is **Kingston**.
wichtigste: The capital city of Jamaica is Kingston.
The official language is **English**.
Jamaica became independent from Britain in 1962.
Reggae comes from Jamaica, and its best-known singer is **Bob Marley**.
**Usain Bolt** holds the world record in the 100 metres (as of 2025).
The flag is green, yellow and black.

abschnitte.text: Jamaica is one of the Greater Antilles in the **Caribbean**. The island is mountainous and green, with beaches on the coast. In the east lie the **Blue Mountains**. There grows a particularly well-known and expensive **coffee**. On the fields people also grow sugar cane and bananas.

First the Taíno lived on Jamaica. Later the Spanish came, and then the island became a British **colony**. The British brought many people from Africa as slaves, who had to work on the sugar cane plantations. In 1962 Jamaica became **independent**. That is why the official language is still **English** today. In everyday life many people speak Patois, a language of its own that is built on English.

**Reggae** arose in Jamaica in the 1960s. It has a slow, swaying rhythm. The most famous reggae musician is **Bob Marley**, whose songs are known all over the world. His music is often about freedom, peace and togetherness.

Jamaica has many world-class sprinters. Best known is **Usain Bolt**, who ran the world record over 100 metres in Berlin in 2009 in 9.58 seconds. This record still stands (as of 2025). Jamaica also became famous in 1988, when a **bobsleigh team** took part in the Winter Olympics in Calgary, although there is never any snow on the island. The story was later made into a film.

gewusst: The flag of Jamaica is one of the few national flags without red, white or blue.
Reggae is on the UNESCO list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

teile.einleitung: The Great Plains are huge, flat plains in the interior of North America. They lie east of the Rocky Mountains and reach from Canada to Texas. A great deal of grain is grown and cattle are kept here.
wichtigste: The Great Plains lie between the Rocky Mountains and the damper regions in the east.
They stretch from Canada in the north to Texas in the south.
The 100th meridian west is regarded as a rough border between the damper east and the drier west.
Centre-pivot irrigation creates the typical round fields.
In the past, huge herds of bison lived here.

abschnitte.text: The Great Plains are a wide, almost treeless **grassland**. Landscapes like this are also called **prairie**. The land rises slowly from east to west towards the **Rocky Mountains**. In the past huge herds of **bison** roamed here, and Indigenous peoples lived by hunting them. Today wheat and maize fields and large cattle pastures shape the landscape.

The further west you go, the less it rains. The **100th meridian west** is traditionally seen as a rough border. East of it, the rain is usually enough for farming. West of it there is mainly **pasture land**, and fields often have to be irrigated. The line is not a sharp border, but a broad transition.

From an aeroplane you can see many **perfectly round green fields** on the Great Plains. They are created by **centre-pivot irrigation**. A long sprinkler arm on wheels turns around a well in the middle. The water often comes from the **Ogallala Aquifer**, a huge store of groundwater. Because more water is taken out than flows back in, the water level is falling in many places.

gewusst: In the 1930s, severe dust storms on the Great Plains carried away so much soil that people spoke of the “Dust Bowl”.
A single round field can have a diameter of almost a kilometre.

teile.einleitung: The Tibetan Plateau is the highest and largest plateau on Earth. It lies on average about 4,500 metres above sea level and is therefore called the “roof of the world”. Many of Asia’s great rivers rise there.
wichtigste: The Tibetan Plateau lies at an average height of about 4,500 m.
It is often called the “roof of the world”.
It was formed by the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate.
Lhasa is the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region.
Since 2006 the Qinghai-Tibet Railway has run over the Tanggula Pass, about 5,070 m high, to Lhasa.
As the “water tower of Asia” it feeds great rivers such as the Indus, the Yellow River and the Brahmaputra.
The yak is especially well adapted to life on the plateau.

abschnitte.text: The **Tibetan Plateau** lies in Central Asia and for the most part belongs to China. It lies on average at about **4,500 metres** above sea level, so higher than almost all the peaks of the Alps. It is the highest and largest plateau on Earth. That is why it is called the **“roof of the world”**, a term also used for the Pamirs. To the south it is bounded by the **Himalayas**.

For about **50 million years** the **Indian Plate** has been pushing north against the **Eurasian Plate**. In this collision the Earth’s crust was squeezed together and lifted up. This is how the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau came into being. The process continues to this day, which is why there are earthquakes in the region too.

Glaciers and snowfields in Tibet feed many great **rivers**, for example the **Indus**, the **Yellow River** and the **Salween**. The **Brahmaputra** also rises in Tibet and flows east there as the **Yarlung Tsangpo**. After that it cuts through the Himalayas in one of the deepest gorges on Earth. Almost two billion people depend on water from this region. That is why the plateau is also called the **“water tower of Asia”**.

**Lhasa** is the capital of the **Tibet Autonomous Region**. It lies at a height of about **3,650 metres**. With the **Potala Palace** it is the traditional centre of Tibet. Since **2006** the **Qinghai-Tibet Railway** has run to Lhasa. It crosses the **Tanggula Pass**, about **5,070 metres** high, and is one of the highest railway lines in the world. A large part runs over **permafrost**, which is kept stable with cooling pipes.

Life on the plateau is hard: the air is thin and the winters are cold. The **yak** is especially well adapted to it. It has a thick coat, large lungs and many red blood cells. For the herders it is very important. It supplies **milk**, **wool**, **meat** and dried dung as **fuel**.

gewusst: The Himalayas grow a little higher every year because of the pressure of the Indian Plate.
On the trains to Lhasa, passengers get extra oxygen because the air is so thin.

teile.einleitung: Industrial location theory explains why factories are built in particular places. It was founded by the economist Alfred Weber in 1909. At its centre are the costs of transporting raw materials and finished products.
wichtigste: In 1909 Alfred Weber published the work “On the Location of Industries”.
According to Weber, a business looks for the place with the lowest transport costs.
The material index is the weight of the localised materials divided by the weight of the product.
If the material index is greater than 1, the location tends to be near the raw material, and if it is less than 1, near the market.
Raw materials that are available everywhere, such as water, are called ubiquities.
Cheap labour and agglomeration advantages can lure a business away from the point of lowest transport costs.

abschnitte.text: The German economist **Alfred Weber** was the brother of the sociologist Max Weber. In **1909** he published the work **“On the Location of Industries”**. With it he founded the classical **industrial location theory**. He assumed that **transport costs** are the most important factor in choosing a location.

Weber distinguishes **localised materials**, which occur only in certain places, from **ubiquities**, which are available almost everywhere, such as water. The **material index** is the weight of the localised materials divided by the weight of the product. If you need 4 tonnes of raw materials for 1 tonne of product, the index is 4. A value above 1 favours a location near the **raw material**, and a value below 1 favours a location near the **sales market**.

Beer consists for the most part of **water**, and water is a ubiquity. The finished beer is therefore much heavier than the raw materials that have to be brought in. The heavy transport to customers is saved if you brew close to the market. That is why in earlier times almost every larger town had its own brewery, in Switzerland too.

To find the best place between two raw material sites and a market, Weber uses the **location triangle**. With **isodapanes** he tests deviations. These are lines that join places with the same additional transport costs. If a place with **cheap labour** lies within a suitable isodapane, moving there pays off. **Agglomeration advantages**, that is, benefits from many businesses in the same place, can also shift the location.

gewusst: Weber’s theory is over 100 years old and is still explained in geography lessons today.
The word “ubiquity” comes from the Latin “ubique”, which means “everywhere”.

teile.einleitung: Ida Pfeiffer was an Austrian traveller from Vienna. In the 19th century she travelled twice around the world as a woman, mostly alone and with little money. She wrote successful books about her travels.
wichtigste: Ida Pfeiffer was born in Vienna in 1797.
She began her great journeys only when her sons were grown up.
Her first journey in 1842 took her to the Holy Land and Egypt.
She travelled twice around the Earth, mostly alone.
She paid for her journeys with books and natural specimens she collected.
Her last journey took her to Madagascar, and she died in Vienna in 1858.

abschnitte.text: Ida Pfeiffer was born in **Vienna** in **1797**. Even as a child she dreamed of faraway lands. For a long time, though, she lived in Vienna as a wife and mother. Only when her **sons were grown up** could she fulfil her dream. In 1842, aged about 44, she set out on her first great journey.

abschnitte.titel: To the Holy Land and the north
abschnitte.text: Her first journey took her via **Constantinople** to **Palestine** and **Egypt**. She wrote a book about it that many people read. In 1845 she travelled to **Iceland** and **Scandinavia** in the far north. She published a travel account about this too.

After that Ida Pfeiffer dared to do something very unusual: she travelled **twice around the Earth**. She visited, among other places, South America, China, India, South-East Asia and North America. Most of the time she travelled **alone** and had little money. She travelled simply, often stayed with local people and took long, difficult routes.

To pay for her journeys she wrote **travel accounts**, which were translated into several languages. She also collected **insects**, **plants** and **rocks** and sold them to museums. Her last journey took her to **Madagascar**. There she fell seriously ill with fever in 1857. She died in 1858 in Vienna after her return.

In the 19th century women hardly ever travelled alone to faraway countries. Ida Pfeiffer showed that **women too can make great journeys of exploration**. That is why she is still seen today as a role model for many later travellers and women scientists.

gewusst: On her journeys Ida Pfeiffer covered many tens of thousands of kilometres, at a time without aeroplanes.
Some animal species that she collected were named after her.

teile.einleitung: The Canadian Shield is a huge region of ancient rock. It covers about half of Canada and is full of lakes, forests and mineral resources.
wichtigste: The Canadian Shield consists of very old rock from the Precambrian.
Parts of it are over 2.5 billion years old.
It covers about half of Canada.
It lies like a horseshoe around Hudson Bay.
Ice Age glaciers left behind countless lakes.
The Shield is rich in ores such as nickel and gold.

abschnitte.text: The Canadian Shield is a **basement complex** of very old rock. It dates from the **Precambrian**, the oldest stretch of Earth’s history. Parts of it are over **2.5 billion years** old. Typical rocks are **gneiss** and **granite**. The Shield forms the geological **core of North America**. Once it was a high mountain range that was worn away over an unimaginably long time.

The Shield covers about **half of Canada**. It stretches from **Labrador** in the east to the **Northwest Territories**. Like a huge horseshoe it surrounds **Hudson Bay**, which lies in a depression in its middle. Small parts also reach into the USA.

In the last **Ice Age** a thick ice sheet lay over the region. The **glaciers** ground down the hard rock and left behind countless **hollows**. In them meltwater and rainwater later collected, and in this way thousands of **lakes** came about. The glaciers also largely stripped away the soil. That is why often only a **thin, stony layer of earth** lies over the rock. This is hardly suitable for farming.

In the old rock lie rich deposits of **nickel**, **gold**, **copper**, **iron** and **uranium**. Well known is the mining near **Sudbury** in Ontario. The many rivers and lakes are well suited to **reservoirs**. In Quebec, for example at the **James Bay Project**, electricity from **hydroelectric power** is produced on a large scale. Quebec generates most of its electricity in this way.

In the south of the Shield grows the **boreal coniferous forest** with spruces, pines and birches. In between lie many swamps and bogs. Further north it gets colder, and the forest passes into the treeless **tundra**. There only mosses, lichens and low shrubs grow.

gewusst: Some of the oldest rocks on Earth have been found in the Canadian Shield.
In Switzerland too, Ice Age glaciers formed lakes, for example many small mountain lakes in the Alps.

teile.einleitung: The cod is a large sea fish from the North Atlantic. For centuries it was one of the most important food fish, and today it shows how dangerous overfishing is.
wichtigste: The cod lives in the cool water of the North Atlantic.
In the Baltic Sea it is called “Dorsch” in German.
For centuries it was a very important food fish.
Off Newfoundland in Canada the stock collapsed in 1992.
The reason for this was overfishing.
Dried cod is called stockfish.

abschnitte.text: The cod lives in the **North Atlantic**, for example off Norway, Iceland and Canada. It likes cool water. On its chin it has a small thread, a so-called **barbel**. With it, it feels for food on the sea floor. It eats smaller fish, crabs and worms. In the Baltic Sea the same fish is called **Dorsch** in German.

Centuries ago, fishermen already went far out to catch cod. Dried, it keeps for a very long time. Air-dried cod is called **stockfish**, and salted and dried cod is called **klippfish**. In this way it could be taken on long sea voyages and sold in many countries. Whole coastal villages lived from catching cod.

Off **Newfoundland** in Canada there used to be an incredible amount of cod. With big fishing ships and modern nets, though, more and more was caught. Too few fish were left to breed. In **1992** Canada had to ban fishing. Many fishermen lost their jobs. The stock is still recovering only very slowly today.

The case of Newfoundland shows what **overfishing** means: more fish are caught than can grow back. Today many countries set **catch quotas**, so that enough fish stay in the sea. Labels on packaging show whether a fish comes from sustainable fishing. In Switzerland too, you can pay attention to this when shopping.

gewusst: Between Iceland and Britain in the 20th century there were even disputes over fishing grounds, the so-called “Cod Wars”.
On the Lofoten Islands in Norway, cod is still dried today in the wind on large wooden racks.

teile.einleitung: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean on Earth, after the Pacific and the Atlantic. It lies between Africa, Asia, Australia and Antarctica. In it lie dream beaches such as the Maldives, but also huge islands such as Madagascar.
wichtigste: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean on Earth.
It borders Africa, Asia, Australia and Antarctica.
The Maldives consist of about 1,200 low coral islands.
Madagascar is a large island off the east coast of Africa.
The monsoon changes direction with the season and brings rainy seasons to South Asia.
In December 2004 an undersea earthquake off Sumatra set off a devastating tsunami.
The Indian Ocean is the warmest of the large oceans.

abschnitte.text: The **Indian Ocean** covers about a fifth of the water surface of the Earth. In the west lies Africa, in the north Asia with India, in the east Australia and in the south Antarctica. It includes marginal seas such as the **Arabian Sea**, the Bay of Bengal and the Red Sea. It is named after India, which juts far into it.

The **Maldives** are an island state of about 1,200 low coral islands, most of them only one to two metres above the sea. **Madagascar**, off the east coast of Africa, is the fourth largest island on Earth and famous for its lemurs, which live only there. Other island states are Sri Lanka, Mauritius and the Seychelles. Many islands are popular holiday destinations with coral reefs.

Over the Indian Ocean blows the **monsoon**, a wind that changes direction with the season. In summer it brings damp air from the sea to India, Bangladesh and South-East Asia, and then the **rainy season** begins. In winter it blows from the land to the sea, and it stays dry. The monsoon rain is vital for farming, especially for growing rice.

On 26 December 2004 a huge undersea earthquake occurred off the island of **Sumatra** in Indonesia. It set off a **tsunami**, a series of giant waves that hit the coasts of many countries. Over 200,000 people died, including in Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand. Holidaymakers from Switzerland also lost their lives, and since then there has been a tsunami warning system for the Indian Ocean.

In the Indian Ocean live whales, dolphins, sea turtles, sharks and countless colourful reef fish. The **coral reefs** are threatened by the warming of the sea, because corals bleach in water that is too warm. Off Madagascar and the Seychelles there are especially many species that occur only there. Mangrove forests on the coasts protect against storm surges.

Over 2,000 years ago, traders were already sailing back and forth between Arabia, East Africa and India with the help of the monsoon winds. They traded in spices, cloth and gemstones. Today oil tankers from the Persian Gulf and container ships from Asia cross the Indian Ocean on their way to Europe. The Strait of Malacca links it with the Pacific.

begriffe.erklaerung: A great wind that changes direction with the season.
A huge wave, usually set off by an undersea earthquake.
An island that has formed from the limestone skeletons of corals.
A wet-nosed primate that lives only on Madagascar.

gewusst: The Maldives are the flattest country in the world, which is why rising sea levels threaten them especially.
The waves of the 2004 tsunami even reached the coast of East Africa, thousands of kilometres away.

teile.einleitung: The record low temperature is the lowest temperature ever measured at a weather station on Earth. It comes from Antarctica, the coldest continent in the world.
wichtigste: The lowest temperature was measured in Antarctica.
In July 1983 the thermometer showed minus 89.2 degrees Celsius.
It was measured at the Russian research station Vostok.
In July it is winter in the Southern Hemisphere.
Antarctica is colder than the Arctic because it lies high up and is covered by thick ice.
The cold record for Switzerland is minus 41.8 degrees in La Brévine.

abschnitte.text: On 21 July 1983 at the **Vostok** station in Antarctica, **minus 89.2 degrees Celsius** was measured. This is the lowest air temperature ever measured at a weather station. For comparison: a freezer compartment is about minus 18 degrees cold. In such cold, exhaled air freezes at once into ice crystals.

The Russian research station Vostok lies about **3,500 metres** up in the middle of the ice of Antarctica. There scientists study the weather and the ancient ice. The record was measured in **winter**, because in July it is winter in the **Southern Hemisphere**. Then the Sun does not shine at all for weeks. Satellites have even detected lower values on the snow surface in Antarctica.

For temperatures below zero, the bigger the number after the **minus**, the colder it is. Minus 40 degrees is therefore colder than minus 10 degrees. **Antarctica** is even colder than the **Arctic** at the North Pole. It is a continent, lies high up and is covered with a layer of ice a kilometre thick. In the Arctic, by contrast, there is sea beneath the ice, and the water warms things up a little.

The lowest officially measured temperature in Switzerland is **minus 41.8 degrees**. It was measured in January 1987 in **La Brévine** in the canton of Neuchâtel. The place lies in a valley in which cold air collects on clear nights. That is why it is also called the “Siberia of Switzerland”.

gewusst: In the Northern Hemisphere, temperatures below minus 67 degrees have been measured in Siberia and Greenland.
At minus 40 degrees, a Celsius and a Fahrenheit thermometer show exactly the same number.

teile.einleitung: Hurricane Harvey hit the coast of Texas in the USA in August 2017. It stayed almost in the same place for days and brought record rainfall. Large parts of the city of Houston were flooded.
wichtigste: Harvey reached the coast of Texas in August 2017 as a strong hurricane.
After landfall the storm stalled for days.
In places more than 1,500 millimetres of rain fell.
Large parts of the Houston region were flooded.
Harvey is one of the costliest natural disasters in the history of the USA.

abschnitte.text: Harvey formed over the Atlantic and quickly grew stronger over very warm water in the **Gulf of Mexico**. At the end of August 2017 it reached the coast of **Texas** as a category 4 hurricane. The moment a storm hits land is called **landfall**. After that the wind weakened, but the rain stayed.

What was special about Harvey was that after landfall it **stalled for days**. It hardly moved on and kept raining over the same region. In places **more than 1,500 millimetres** of rain fell. That is more than falls in a whole year in many parts of Switzerland.

The big city of **Houston** was hit especially hard. Streets turned into rivers, and tens of thousands of homes stood under water. Many people had to be rescued with boats and helicopters. Harvey is one of the **costliest natural disasters** in the history of the USA. The name Harvey will therefore not be used again for future storms.

gewusst: Harvey brought the most rain ever measured in the USA from a tropical storm.

teile.einleitung: The emperor penguin is the biggest penguin in the world. It lives in the icy Antarctic and, of all times, breeds in the dark, cold winter.
wichtigste: The emperor penguin is the biggest species of penguin and grows over a metre tall.
It lives only around Antarctica.
On its neck it has yellow-orange patches.
It cannot fly, but swims and dives very well.
The father keeps the egg warm on his feet.
In a storm the penguins huddle close together.

abschnitte.text: The **emperor penguin** is the biggest of all species of penguin. It grows over a metre tall and is heavily built. Its back is black and its belly white. On its neck and ears it has **yellow-orange patches**. A thick layer of fat and dense feathers protect it from the cold.

Emperor penguins live only around **Antarctica** at the South Pole. At the North Pole there are no penguins. In winter the temperatures there fall far below zero, and icy storms sweep over the ice. In such weather many penguins **huddle close together** and warm each other. In doing so they keep moving from the cold edge into the warm middle.

Emperor penguins breed in the middle of **winter**, when it is almost always dark. The female lays a single egg and hands it to the male. The **father** carries the egg on his **feet** and covers it with a warm fold of skin on his belly. For about two months he stands like this on the ice and eats nothing. The mother goes to feed in the sea during this time and comes back later to feed the chick.

Penguins are **birds**, but they cannot fly. Their wings have become strong **flippers**. With them they swim fast through the water. Emperor penguins dive deep into the sea and hunt **fish**, **squid** and small crustaceans. Their streamlined body glides well through the water as they do so.

gewusst: Emperor penguins can dive several hundred metres deep.
While the father keeps the egg warm, he loses a lot of weight, because he eats nothing for weeks.

teile.einleitung: Hong Kong is a huge city on the south coast of China with many skyscrapers and one of the biggest ports in the world. For a long time Hong Kong was a British colony. Since 1997 it has belonged to China again, but has a special status.
wichtigste: Hong Kong became British in 1842 after the First Opium War.
On 1 July 1997 Britain returned Hong Kong to China.
Hong Kong is a special administrative region under the principle of “One country, two systems”.
This special status was guaranteed for 50 years, until 2047.
People pay with the Hong Kong dollar.
In everyday life most people speak Cantonese.
China’s second special administrative region is Macau.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century Britain fought China in the **First Opium War**. After the British victory, China had to cede the island of Hong Kong in the **Treaty of Nanking** in 1842. Later the **Kowloon** peninsula was added. In 1898 Britain also leased the **New Territories** for 99 years. A small place became an important trading city.

The lease for the New Territories ran out in 1997. Without this area Hong Kong would hardly have been able to survive. So in 1984 Britain and China agreed in the **Joint Declaration** to hand back the whole colony. On 1 July 1997 Hong Kong became part of the People’s Republic of China.

Hong Kong is a **special administrative region**. Under the principle of **“One country, two systems”** it has its own law, its own border controls and its own currency, the **Hong Kong dollar**. These rules were guaranteed for 50 years, that is, until 2047. In recent years China has greatly increased its influence, which led to large protests in Hong Kong.

Between **Hong Kong Island** and Kowloon lies **Victoria Harbour**. Kowloon is one of the most densely populated places in the world. In everyday life people speak **Cantonese**, and the official languages are Chinese and English. Since 2018 a bridge and tunnel link about 55 kilometres long has joined Hong Kong with Zhuhai and **Macau**.

gewusst: Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than almost any other city in the world.
Macau used to be Portuguese and was handed back to China in 1999.

teile.einleitung: **Iceland** is an island in the North Atlantic, just below the Arctic Circle. It is a land of fire and ice: there are many volcanoes, hot springs and large glaciers. The capital city is **Reykjavík**.
wichtigste: Iceland lies on the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**, where two continental plates drift apart.
That is why there are many volcanoes and earthquakes in Iceland.
The heat from the ground is used mainly to heat houses.
In **Thingvellir** National Park you can see the rift between the plates.
In 2010 the ash from Eyjafjallajökull brought air traffic in Europe to a standstill.
The island of Surtsey newly formed in the sea from 1963.

abschnitte.titel: A land on the seam of the Earth
abschnitte.text: Right through Iceland runs the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**. Here the North American and Eurasian Plates drift apart by about two centimetres every year. Magma rises from the cracks. In addition there is a **hotspot** under Iceland, a particularly hot place in the Earth’s mantle. That is why Iceland is one of the regions of the world richest in volcanoes.

**Hekla** erupted so often that in the Middle Ages it was called the “Gateway to Hell”. In 1783 the fissure **Laki** opened. Lava flowed from it for months, and poisonous gases drifted over Europe. Crops failed and famines followed. In 2010 **Eyjafjallajökull** hurled so much ash into the air that many aeroplanes in Europe had to stay on the ground for days.

In 1963 a volcanic eruption in the sea began off the south coast. From it came the island of **Surtsey**. Researchers may set foot on it, but nobody else. In this way you can observe exactly how plants and animals settle a completely new island. Today Surtsey is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Iceland uses **geothermal energy**. Hot water from underground is led through pipes to the houses and heats the greatest part of the homes. In addition, almost all of the electricity is produced from this and from hydroelectric power. Also famous are the spouting springs: the **Geysir** in the south gave all geysers in the world their name.

In **Thingvellir** National Park you can see deep rifts in the rock where the two continental plates move apart. Here from the year 930 the **Althing** gathered, the assembly of the Icelanders. It counts as one of the oldest parliaments in the world. Thingvellir is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: In the Silfra rift in Thingvellir you can dive between two continental plates.
Iceland’s biggest glacier, Vatnajökull, is among the biggest glaciers in Europe.

teile.einleitung: On Earth there are huge lakes that almost seem like seas. Some are salty, others contain fresh water. Here you will get to know the largest lakes in the world, in Europe and in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake on Earth, about nine times as big as Switzerland.
Lake Ladoga is the largest lake in Europe, and Lake Onega is the second largest.
Lake Titicaca is regarded as the highest navigable lake on Earth.
Great Bear Lake is the largest lake lying entirely in Canada.
Lake Eyre in Australia is almost dried out most of the time.
Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The largest lake on Earth is the **Caspian Sea** between Europe and Asia. Despite its name it is a lake, because it has no connection to the ocean. Its water is slightly salty. It has an area of about 370,000 to 390,000 square kilometres. Switzerland measures about 41,000 square kilometres, so the Caspian Sea is **about nine times** as big.

The largest lake in Europe is **Lake Ladoga** in Russia, north-east of Saint Petersburg. It has an area of about 17,700 square kilometres, almost half as much as Switzerland. The second largest is **Lake Onega**, also in the north-west of Russia. It has almost 10,000 square kilometres. The two lakes are connected to each other by rivers and canals.

**Lake Titicaca** lies in the Andes at about 3810 metres above sea level. It is regarded as the **highest navigable lake** on Earth. Ships and boats made of reeds sail on it. **Great Bear Lake** in Canada lies near the Arctic Circle and is frozen for many months of the year. It is the largest lake lying entirely in Canada. In Russia lies **Lake Baikal**, the deepest lake on Earth.

**Lake Eyre** in Australia, also called **Kati Thanda**, is the largest lake on the continent. Most of the time, though, it is almost dried out. Then you see only a wide, white **crust of salt**. Only after rare, heavy rainfalls does it fill with water. Then many birds come to feed and breed there.

The largest lake lying **entirely in Switzerland** is **Lake Neuchâtel**, with about 218 square kilometres. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are bigger. But Switzerland shares them with its neighbouring countries, as it does Lake Maggiore. Compared with the giants of the world, Swiss lakes are small, but often very deep and clear.

gewusst: The Caspian Sea is called a “sea”, but it is the largest lake on Earth.
Lake Eyre lies below sea level and is mostly a salt desert.

teile.einleitung: Kamchatka is a large peninsula in the far east of Russia. It is famous for its many volcanoes, hot springs and brown bears catching salmon.
wichtigste: Kamchatka belongs to Russia and lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire.
On the peninsula there are over 160 volcanoes, about 30 of them active.
The highest volcano is Klyuchevskaya Sopka.
In the west lies the Sea of Okhotsk, and in the east the Pacific and the Bering Sea.
In the Valley of Geysers, hot water shoots out of the ground.
The capital Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky has no road link to the rest of Russia.

abschnitte.text: Kamchatka lies on the **Pacific Ring of Fire**. Off the east coast the **Pacific Plate** sinks beneath another tectonic plate in the Kuril-Kamchatka Trench. In the process magma forms and rises. That is why there are over **160 volcanoes**, about **30** of them active. The highest is **Klyuchevskaya Sopka** at about 4,750 metres. It is considered the highest active volcano in Eurasia.

A **geyser** is a hot spring that again and again shoots a fountain of water into the air. In the **Valley of Geysers** there are about 90 of them. It is among the biggest geyser fields in the world.
